corroborations.title: Drawer and panel resizing snaps back; default timing/test-vector content is unusably short
corroborations.verification: Fresh live divider drags and vector run, backed by source.
corroborations.observed: Both tested divider positions remain unchanged after dragging. Timing shows only the ruler; loaded test vectors report 2 passed/2 failed but have no visible result rows at the default drawer height.
reproduction: Open Timing diagram and select clk.
Drag the drawer divider upward and the Circuits divider rightward.
Open inv > Test Vector and load the copied inv_test.txt.
corroborations.rootCause: Continuous split layout reapplies the remembered size before drag release can persist the new size. Drawer migration/minimum is in unscaled pixels, so the existing height is inadequate at 1.6.
corroborations.fix: Apply restored sizes during initialization/explicit relayout only, permit live dragging, and persist the released size. Derive the drawer's initial/minimum useful height from its controls and font metrics; keep body scrolling available.
corroborations.acceptance: At 1.0, 1.6 and 2.0 scales, drag every splitter smoothly, reopen with sizes retained, and inspect a visible waveform plus at least four test rows. A 2-pass/2-fail vector exposes each failed cell and Show/Set actions.
corroborations.reason: Same shared splitter defect as shell-03. Hidden timing/test rows are downstream effects, not two extra bugs.

corroborations.title: Circuit list loses its listener to garbage collection and becomes stale
corroborations.verification: Fresh live GC, tab-switch and F2 rename; source establishes lifetime defect.
corroborations.observed: After jcmd GC.run on the private JVM, main is active while inv remains selected in the list. Renaming osc to osc_qa updates the tab and title while the list still displays osc.
reproduction: Open main and inv from the list.
Allow GC or request GC only on a disposable QA JVM.
Click main tab and compare list highlight.
Select osc, press F2, rename to osc_qa; compare row and tab.
corroborations.rootCause: MyListener is a constructor-local variable registered with weak project/library event sources. CircuitListView does not retain it strongly.
corroborations.fix: Retain the listener in a field for the view lifetime, unregister on disposal, and keep current-circuit selection and library mutations synchronized. Guard actions against targets no longer in the project.
corroborations.acceptance: After forced GC, add/rename/delete/reorder/set-main and tab switching update the list immediately. Undo/redo does the same. A deleted row cannot be reopened as a ghost.
corroborations.reason: Unifies add/rename, stale highlight, and recovered deleted-row symptoms. No data-loss claim: ghost editing/saving was not retested.

corroborations.title: Chronogram ruler baseline clips timestamp and cursor text
corroborations.verification: Fresh ruler crop and recovered populated waveform crop actually viewed; current code checked.
corroborations.observed: The tops of timestamps and the highlighted cursor label disappear above the ruler. This remains visible in recovered images with a taller drawer.
reproduction: Open Timing diagram at 1.6.
Generate ticks and inspect the ruler at native pixels; enlarge drawer after fixing the splitter.
corroborations.rootCause: Fixed 20-pixel header and h/2 baseline are incompatible with the scaled monospaced font.
corroborations.fix: Compute header/row dimensions and baselines from font ascent/descent and scaled padding. Size signal-name/value columns for useful content.
corroborations.acceptance: Ruler and cursor labels are entirely inside their bounds at all supported scales, with no overlap at minimum and enlarged drawer sizes.
corroborations.reason: Visual corroboration of the existing codeaudit-08 cause; not another drawer-resize bug.

findings.title: Build Circuit defaults to overwriting the circuit being analyzed; two keystrokes replace the user's circuit

originalClaim.title: Build Circuit defaults to overwriting the circuit being analyzed; two keystrokes replace the user's circuit
originalClaim.surface: Analyzer > Build Circuit dialog + Confirm Replace dialog
originalClaim.observed: The Circuit Name field is prefilled with the analyzed circuit's own name (FULLADDER). Keyboard focus is NOT in that field: typing 'Q' does nothing. OK is the default button, so Space or Enter confirms. The follow-up 'Are you sure you want to replace the circuit FULLADDER?' has Yes as the default button. When I typed a new name straight into the dialog, the space in it pressed OK, Enter then accepted Yes, and the user's FULLADDER circuit was replaced by the generated gates. It was recoverable only through the main window's Edit > Undo Replace Circuit, which the dialogs never mention.
originalClaim.expected: A non-destructive default: a new unique name such as 'FULLADDER_built', with the field focused and its text selected. If the name collides, the confirmation should use explicit 'Replace' / 'Cancel' buttons with Cancel as the default, and say that the action can be undone.
originalClaim.repro: Analyze FULLADDER > Build Circuit > type 'FA built' without clicking the field (the space presses OK) > Enter (accepts Yes) > FULLADDER now contains the generated circuit.
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/gui/BuildCircuitButton.java:69-72 prefills name with model.getCurrentCircuit().getName(). :142-147 shows the form through OptionPane.showConfirmDialog, so initial focus goes to the OK button, not the name field. :195-199 uses a YES_NO confirm with Yes as the default. The string replaceCircuitAction ('Replace Circuit') exists in analyze.properties but is not used.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Build a proper dialog: focus the name field (requestFocusInWindow on show); default the name to a unique '<name>_built'; make the primary button say 'Build'; on a name collision, show an inline warning under the field ('Replaces existing circuit FULLADDER — can be undone') instead of a second modal, or at least use 'Replace' / 'Cancel' with Cancel as the default.

review.title: Build Circuit defaults to overwriting the circuit being analyzed; two keystrokes replace the user's circuit
review.reason: Initial Q typing did not change FULLADDER. Space then Enter replaced its layout. Undo restored the original layout and clean title. This is an unsafe, recoverable default; no irreversible or saved-file loss demonstrated.

findings.title: Overlines float ~8px above the letters and are shifted left, so negated variables are ambiguous

originalClaim.title: Overlines float ~8px above the letters and are shifted left, so negated variables are ambiguous
originalClaim.surface: Simplified tab minimized expression; K-map 'Selected group' box; Expression tab (Mathematical notation)
originalClaim.observed: In a'·b'·c + a'·b·c' + … the overline bars sit ~8 px above the x-height with a clear gap, and each bar starts about one glyph-width left of its variable. In POS form, the bar meant for 'a' in '(a'+b+c')' covers '(' and half of the 'a'. In the Selected-group box the bars are crammed into the box edge.
originalClaim.expected: Overlines 1–2 px above the tallest glyph of exactly the negated span, horizontally aligned with the glyphs, at a consistent stroke width.
originalClaim.repro: Analyze FULLADDER > Simplified tab > look at the expression under the K-map (SOP and POS).
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/data/ExpressionRenderData.java:66 sets notSep = getScaled(3), then :214 and :372 apply getScaled(notSep) again. The overline gap is therefore scaled twice (3 × 1.6 × 1.6 ≈ 7.7 px), and the bar is drawn at the top of the line box (lineY) rather than at the glyph ascent. The horizontal start/stop are measured by getWidth(ctx, …) at :340-343, which does not match the positions produced by drawString(as.getIterator()) at :367, so every bar is offset left.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Remove the double scaling: use notSep directly and compute notY from baseline − ascent − depth·notSep. Measure start/stop with a TextLayout of the same AttributedString that is drawn (TextLayout.getCaretShape or getLogicalHighlightShape), not a separately styled substring. Add a render test that checks the overline x-range against the glyph bounds.

review.title: Overlines float ~8px above the letters and are shifted left, so negated variables are ambiguous
review.reason: Personally inspected recovered overline crop: bars have excessive gap and mismatched horizontal spans. HEAD double-scales notSep; the precise horizontal metric failure remains a hypothesis.

findings.title: K-map covers in dark theme: white digits on pale olive/tan covers at 1.9:1 contrast, muddy overlaps, cover box offset from its digit

originalClaim.title: K-map covers in dark theme: white digits on pale olive/tan covers at 1.9:1 contrast, muddy overlaps, cover box offset from its digit
originalClaim.surface: Simplified tab K-map (dark theme), both Numbered and Lined styles
originalClaim.observed: Cover fills are pastel palette colours at alpha 180 over #1E1F22, which gives #AAAD2B olive, #AE9C68 tan, #AE6768 dusty pink and #AD4E2B rust, all drawn with light text #E2E6ED. Measured contrast: 1.92:1 on olive, 2.16:1 on tan, 3.4:1 on pink. Overlapping covers blend into brownish mud (orange over tan and pink). Each rounded cover sits ~2 px higher than its digit, so the '1' hangs over the cover's bottom edge. When a group is hovered, the other covers turn grey and the Selected-group box fills with a muddy maroon.
originalClaim.expected: Cover colours designed for dark UI: saturated outlines or low-alpha fills with the digit staying fully legible (≥4.5:1). Distinct outline strokes for overlapping groups, and covers centred on the cell.
originalClaim.repro: Dark theme > analyze FULLADDER > Simplified tab.
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/data/KarnaughMapGroups.java:135-161 fills covers with adjustColor(color, 128, 180) at alpha 180 in dark mode, and :140 greys other groups with (170,170,170,160). The palette at src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/prefs/AppPreferences.java:735-752 (DARK_KMAP_COLORS) contains light tints such as 0xEAD186 and 0xE4E830, and the cell text colour DARK_KMAP_CELL_TEXT_COLOR 0xFFE2E6ED at :755 is also light. The fillRoundRect insets (IMP_INSET) are not aligned with the digit baseline in KarnaughMapPanel.doPaintKMap.
originalClaim.fixIdea: In dark mode draw covers as 2 px coloured outlines with a ~25% alpha fill, or pick the text colour per cover by luminance. Validate against 4.5:1 in KarnaughPaletteTest. Centre the cover rectangle on the cell's text bounds.

review.title: K-map covers in dark theme: white digits on pale olive/tan covers at 1.9:1 contrast, muddy overlaps, cover box offset from its digit
review.reason: Light digits on olive/tan covers are visibly weak in recovered and live maps. Original exact contrast ratios were not independently remeasured.

findings.title: K-map does not scale with the window; header labels shrunk to ~2/3 size; huge dead space

originalClaim.title: K-map does not scale with the window; header labels shrunk to ~2/3 size; huge dead space
originalClaim.surface: Simplified tab
originalClaim.observed: The K-map is ~150 px wide (cells ~36 px) at every window size, including maximized 2560x1600, where it floats in the middle of an empty panel. The Gray-code headers '00 01 11 10' and the row labels '0/1' are drawn at about two-thirds of the UI font size (~12 px at 1.6 scale).
originalClaim.expected: The K-map fills the available space up to a sensible cap, with headers at least at body size, like a diagram viewer.
originalClaim.repro: Simplified tab > maximize the window.
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/gui/KarnaughMapPanel.java:596-600 derives numberFont = headerFont * (width('00')/width('000')) ≈ 0.67×. The cell size comes from font metrics in computePreferredSize (~:200-260), not from the available area. MinimizedTab uses fixed GridBag insets (20,0,20,0) at MinimizedTab.java:310.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Compute cellWidth/cellHeight from the panel size (clamped, e.g. 48–120 px), render the headers at body size, and let the panel take all the space the tab can give it.

review.title: K-map does not scale with the window; header labels shrunk to ~2/3 size; huge dead space
review.reason: Live map remains small with reduced header type, but expansion to fill a large window is a design choice, not a demonstrated failure.

findings.title: No undo anywhere in the analyzer; K-map clicks silently edit the truth table and rewrite the expression

originalClaim.title: No undo anywhere in the analyzer; K-map clicks silently edit the truth table and rewrite the expression
originalClaim.surface: All analyzer tabs; Edit menu
originalClaim.observed: None of these can be undone: truth-table edits, K-map cell toggles, adding or deleting variables, editing expressions. The analyzer's Edit menu reads 'Nothing to Undo' and Ctrl+Z does nothing. A single click on a K-map cell flips its truth-table value (0→1), recomputes the covers and replaces output x's expression on the Expression tab with the new minimal form. There is no hint that cells are editable and no way to get the old function back.
originalClaim.expected: Full undo/redo for analyzer edits, as in any modern editor. K-map editing that is either opt-in (an explicit edit mode) or clearly signalled (a pointer cursor and a tooltip such as 'Click to cycle 0/1/−'), and undoable.
originalClaim.repro: Table tab: type 1 into a cell, then Ctrl+Z (nothing happens). Simplified tab: click a '0' cell; it becomes 1 and the Expression tab changes.
originalClaim.rootCause: The analyze package has no undo support at all (grep 'undo' in src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze returns nothing). KarnaughMapPanel.java:1039-1052 mouseClicked calls tt.setOutputEntry(...) directly. AnalyzerMenuListener only wires the cut/copy/paste/delete edit handlers.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Add an UndoManager to AnalyzerModel that records TruthTable/VariableList/OutputExpressions changes as compound edits, and wire Edit > Undo/Redo and Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z in the analyzer frame. On the K-map, show a hover tooltip and a pointer cursor, or require a double-click or modifier to edit.

review.title: No undo anywhere in the analyzer; K-map clicks silently edit the truth table and rewrite the expression
review.reason: HEAD directly cycles truth-table entries on map clicks; no undo references found in analyze package. Did not independently reproduce all variable/expression edits or irreversible loss.

findings.title: With more than 6 inputs, the Expression and Simplified tabs are disabled without explanation, and the Simplify result can't be viewed anywhere

originalClaim.title: With more than 6 inputs, the Expression and Simplified tabs are disabled without explanation, and the Simplify result can't be viewed anywhere
originalClaim.surface: Tab strip; 'Simplify (sum of products)' / 'Simplify (product of sums)' buttons
originalClaim.observed: For the 8-input main circuit, 'Expression' and 'Simplified' are greyed out. Their tooltip is the generic 'View and manipulate outputs' expressions.' with no reason given. After running Simplify (SOP) and closing the progress dialog, both tabs are still disabled, so the optimized expression cannot be seen anywhere (only indirectly through Build Circuit). Conversely, for ≤6 inputs both Simplify buttons are permanently greyed with no tooltip explaining that minimization is automatic.
originalClaim.expected: Disabled tabs explain why ('Available for up to 6 inputs — this circuit has 8. Use Simplify to compute expressions.'). After Simplify, the Expression tab opens and shows the result. Buttons that are never applicable should be hidden, or at least explained.
originalClaim.repro: Analyze PC.circ 'main' (8 input bits) > hover Expression > Simplify (sum of products) > Yes > close the dialog > Expression is still disabled.
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/gui/Analyzer.java:116-137 (TableListener.update) enables the tabs only for inputs ≤ Implicant.MAXIMAL_NR_OF_INPUTS_FOR_AUTO_MINIMAL_FORM (6, Implicant.java:409) and enables the Simplify buttons only above it. findings.title: Optimizer: debug-log progress dialog, 'click here to close window' button, no Cancel for an 'hours'-long job; warning defaults to Yes

originalClaim.title: Optimizer: debug-log progress dialog, 'click here to close window' button, no Cancel for an 'hours'-long job; warning defaults to Yes
originalClaim.surface: Simplify (SOP/POS) > 'Optimizing logic function' warning and progress dialogs
originalClaim.observed: The warning reads 'Warning, optimizing logic functions with this number of inputs can take a long time (hours)! Do you want to continue?'. It uses a question icon and Yes is the default button. The progress dialog is a raw monospace JTextArea dumping prime-implicant bit strings ('-1---000 -00--01- …'), with a full-width flat button 'Finished optimizing logic function, click here to close window.'. It cannot be cancelled: the close X does nothing (DO_NOTHING_ON_CLOSE) and it is modal. It opens with its top-left corner at the screen centre, off-centre from the analyzer.
originalClaim.expected: A progress sheet with a determinate or indeterminate bar, a human status line ('Minimizing x[3] — 2 of 4 outputs'), a Cancel button, and details collapsed behind a 'Show log' disclosure. A warning icon, with Cancel or 'Don't optimize' as the default for a potentially hours-long job.
originalClaim.repro: Analyze PC.circ main (8 inputs) or INC16 (16) > Simplify (sum of products).
originalClaim.rootCause: src/main/java/com/cburch/logisim/analyze/gui/MinimizeButton.java:41-89. showConfirmDialog YES_NO has no default-button choice and no warning type. JTextArea(20,80) is the log. There is no cancel path into OutputExpressions.forcedOptimize. setLocationRelativeTo(parent) is called before pack() (so the top-left lands at the centre), and infoPanel.setVisible(true) is called from a plain Thread rather than the EDT.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Replace with a SwingWorker-driven progress dialog (EDT-safe) that has a Cancel button honoured by forcedOptimize via an interrupted flag. Pack before setLocationRelativeTo. Use WARNING_MESSAGE with explicit 'Optimize' / 'Cancel' options and Cancel as the default. Collapse the log.

review.title: Optimizer: debug-log progress dialog, 'click here to close window' button, no Cancel for an 'hours'-long job; warning defaults to Yes
review.reason: A running optimizer has DO_NOTHING_ON_CLOSE, hidden done button until completion, no cancellation path here, and Swing changes on raw threads. No hours-long optimization was run; severity applies if a long optimization is entered.

findings.title: Canvas '100%' ignores the 1.6 UI scale – circuits, values and labels render at 1/1.6 size and files open tiny

originalClaim.title: Canvas '100%' ignores the 1.6 UI scale – circuits, values and labels render at 1/1.6 size and files open tiny
originalClaim.surface: Circuit canvas (all circuits, new and opened)
originalClaim.observed: At the default 100% a medium AND gate is 50x50 px and an input pin is 20x10 px, with a value digit ~6 px tall and a radix letter ~4 px. Labels like 'A'/'G1' are ~10 px, against ~22 px UI text right next to them. New circuits start at 100%. Opening PC.circ shows the main circuit as a ~100x40 px speck in the top-left corner and MUX4WAY16 at ~30% of the viewport width, with unreadable 'MUX16'/'b in' text.
originalClaim.expected: Canvas 100% should mean 'same physical scale as the UI' (1 circuit unit = 1.6 device px at scale 1.6), and opened circuits should fit/center at a readable zoom.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Frame.java:255-260 builds the layout BasicZoomModel from AppPreferences.LAYOUT_ZOOM (prefs/AppPreferences.java:1300-1301, default 1.0). Canvas transforms (gui/main/Canvas.java getZoomFactor ~519) never multiply by UiScale. gui/generic/ZoomControl.java:177-181 computeInitialZoomFactor returns Math.min(1.0, fit), so a small circuit never opens above 100%. The default template also stores zoom 1.0 (resources/logisim/default.templ:22).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Apply UiScale as a base factor in the canvas transform (effective = zoom * UiScale.get()) and keep displaying 'zoom' relative to it. Hit-testing, repaint rects and GridPainter must use the same effective factor. Change computeInitialZoomFactor to fit and center (allow >1, clamp to e.g. 1x–2.5x) and center the view.

originalClaim.title: Palette tiles are fixed 68x62 device px, so every component caption is cut in half and truncated to about 5 characters
originalClaim.surface: Side panel > LIBRARY component palette (every tile)
originalClaim.observed: At scale 1.6 each caption shows only the top half of its glyphs (e.g. 'NOT', 'Buffer', 'AND' reduced to ascender stubs, crop-palette.png / t1-menu-z.png). Arithmetic: the tile is HEIGHT=62 and PREVIEW_HEIGHT=40, unscaled. The caption font is UiFonts.small() = round(13*0.85*1.6) = 18px. The baseline is drawn at 40 + Spacing.sm() (13) + ascent (~19) - 2 = ~70px, which is 8px below the tile's bottom edge, so the x-height falls outside the clip. Usable width is 68 - 2*Spacing.xs() = 56px, about 5 glyphs at 18px, so 'Controlled Buffer', 'Pull Resistor' etc. collapse to 'Cont…'. The preview icon is scaled (BOX_SIZE 20*1.6 = 32px) inside the unscaled 40px slot, so it sits 10px from the top with no room below. The favourite star is AppIcons 10 (16px) at literal (width-14, 4). The hover/selection round rect uses arc 8 and stroke 1f/1.6f, unscaled.
originalClaim.expected: Every component name is fully readable at any interface scale. Tile geometry comes from the scale and the caption FontMetrics, and long names wrap to a second line.

The tile never consults FontMetrics for its own size.

Wrap the name onto up to 2 lines, ellipsizing only the second. Scale the star, arc and stroke. Once codeaudit-02 lands, use FlatLaf UIScale.scale(). Add a unit test asserting baseline + descent <= tile height at scales 1.0, 1.25, 1.6 and 2.0.

findings.title: FlatLaf's own UI scale is never set: every metric FlatLaf paints stays at 1x while text is 1.6x

originalClaim.title: FlatLaf's own UI scale is never set: every metric FlatLaf paints stays at 1x while text is 1.6x
originalClaim.surface: Whole application: title bar, menus, trees, tables, tabs, scroll bars, split panes, check boxes, combos, tooltips, text fields
originalClaim.observed: Nothing sets flatlaf.uiScale (FlatSystemProperties.UI_SCALE). FlatLaf therefore auto-detects its scale from the platform font, which gives 1.0 in this Xwayland session: Label.font = 13px, consistent with the 18px UiFonts.small() captions (13*0.85*1.6). Every size FlatLaf takes from FlatLaf.properties or its own defaults is therefore unscaled: Tree/Table rowHeight 24; TabbedPane.tabHeight 32 with tabInsets 4,12; ScrollBar.width 12 (the palette scrollbar is a sliver next to 22px text, crop-palette.png); SplitPane.dividerSize 5; Component.arc/focusWidth; MenuBar.itemMargins 4,10; PopupMenu.borderInsets; ToolTip.borderInsets 4,8 (cramped tooltips). The same holds for the title-bar minimise/maximise/close glyphs (tiny, top right of probe-01.png), check-box and radio icons (about 15px next to 22px labels), combo/spinner arrow buttons, the submenu arrow next to 'Open Recent' (t2-menu-z.png), tree expand chevrons, the text-field clear button and tab close buttons.
originalClaim.expected: One scale authority, so text, row heights, paddings, icons and window chrome all grow together.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/theme/Theme.java:104-122 calls LogisimDarkLaf/LogisimLightLaf.setup() with no scale configured, and Main.java:38-40 never sets flatlaf.uiScale. All values in resources/.../gui/theme/FlatLaf.properties are 1x design values that only FlatLaf's UIScale multiplies. flatlaf-3.7.2 bytecode confirms FlatTableUI/FlatTreeUI install rowHeight = UIScale.scale(24). The app instead scales text separately (codeaudit-03) and custom widgets by hand (UiScale).
originalClaim.fixIdea: In Main, before Theme.install(): System.setProperty("flatlaf.uiScale", String.valueOf(AppPreferences.SCALE_FACTOR.get())). Then make that the only scale. Delete the Startup font listener (codeaudit-03). Make UiScale.factor() return com.formdev.flatlaf.util.UIScale.getUserScaleFactor(). Pass unscaled sizes to FlatSVGIcon in AppIcons, since it scales itself. Change UiFonts to use the (already scaled) Label.font without multiplying again. A scale change in Preferences then needs a restart prompt.

review.reason: Independent app scaling and LaF metrics are the same mismatch documented in scaling-01. FlatLaf can scale via its own font/zoom paths, so 'never scales' is not globally true.

findings.title: A global AWT listener forces every added JLabel/JButton/JMenuItem/... to 14x scale (22.4px), which flattens the type hierarchy and makes it depend on call order

originalClaim.title: A global AWT listener forces every added JLabel/JButton/JMenuItem/... to 14x scale (22.4px), which flattens the type hierarchy and makes it depend on call order
originalClaim.surface: Everywhere; most visible on the Welcome page, status bar, zoom pill, explorer vs labels
originalClaim.observed: Startup registers a CONTAINER_EVENT listener. When a JButton, JCheckBox, JComboBox, JToolTip, JLabel, JMenuItem, JRadioButton, JProgressBar, JSpinner, JTabbedPane, JTextField, JTextArea, JHelp, JFileChooser or JScrollPane (and, recursively, all of its children) is added anywhere, its font is replaced by getScaledFont(font) = font.deriveFont(14*scale). The requested size is discarded. At 1.6 that is 22.4px, unless the code happens to call setFont after add(). Consequences: WelcomePanel hints ('Start from the default template') and recent-file paths are set to UiFonts.small() before add(), so they render as large as the link text (probe-01.png). StatusBar breadcrumbs and separators (small, then add) are 22px while the other status labels (add, then small) are 18px. The ZoomPill percent is 22px beside an 18px status bar. UiFonts.body() is 21px while forced labels are 22.4px, so there are two different body sizes (explorer list vs panel labels). Callers asking for a smaller font get 22.4 anyway: PlaTable smallFont/tinyFont, CpuDrawSupport, Pin editor, KarnaughMapPanel, VariableTab italic.
originalClaim.expected: A deliberate type ramp (caption < body < heading) that survives regardless of when a component is added.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:940-941 (addAWTEventListener) and :1160-1190 (eventDispatched). prefs/AppPreferences.java:392-404 (setScaledFonts) and :446-460 (getScaledFont ignores the incoming font size; FONT_SIZE=14 at :520, while FlatLaf's base is 13). Examples: WelcomePanel.java:156-165, StatusBar.java:120-143, ZoomPill.java:68-80.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Remove the listener and setScaledFonts entirely once FlatLaf owns the scale (codeaudit-02). Replace getScaledFont(...) call sites with UiFonts roles (body/small/heading/mono) that derive relative to Label.font. Add a checkstyle/grep rule banning getScaledFont and deriveFont(<literal>) in UI packages.

review.reason: Global COMPONENT_ADDED listener replaces specified roles with constant 14*Scale. UiFonts derives a different ramp from Label.font. Order-dependent hierarchy loss is real.

findings.title: Menu shortcuts render at ~13px beside 22px menu items, and some read 'Ctrl+Comma'

originalClaim.surface: Every menu (File, Edit, Project, Simulate, ...) and context menus
originalClaim.observed: In the File menu at 1.6 the item labels are about 22px but the right-aligned accelerators ('Ctrl+N', 'Ctrl+Shift+W', ...) are unscaled grey text at roughly 60% of that height. review.reason: Menu label/accelerator mismatch is a symptom of uncoordinated scale. Ctrl+Comma wording is cosmetic.

findings.title: Latent double scaling: AppIcons and UiFonts multiply by the app scale on top of FlatLaf's scale

originalClaim.title: Latent double scaling: AppIcons and UiFonts multiply by the app scale on top of FlatLaf's scale
originalClaim.surface: All SVG interface icons and UiFonts text, on any desktop where FlatLaf detects a scale > 1
originalClaim.observed: AppIcons builds new FlatSVGIcon(res, UiScale.scaled(size), ...), but FlatSVGIcon.getIconWidth() applies UIScale.scale() again (verified in flatlaf-extras 3.7.2 bytecode). UiFonts multiplies UIManager Label.font, which FlatLaf has already sized from the desktop font, by UiScale again. getPlatformScaleFactor() only checks the Java2D transform. On GNOME with text-scaling 1.5, KDE with forceFontDPI, or an Xft.dpi of 144, FlatLaf's scale is 1.5 while Java2D is 1.0, so auto-scale can still pick 1.6. Icons and UiFonts text then come out at 2.4x while listener-forced labels are 1.6x. Today's rig does not hit this; users will.
originalClaim.expected: Exactly one multiplication between design units and device pixels.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/theme/AppIcons.java:156-166 (UiScale.scaled then FlatSVGIcon scales again); util/UiFonts.java:251-260 (scaled base font times UiScale); prefs/AppPreferences.java:1003-1034 (platform scale check ignores FlatLaf's font-derived scale).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Resolved by codeaudit-02. Set flatlaf.uiScale explicitly (this also stops FlatLaf auto-detecting), pass design sizes to FlatSVGIcon, and have UiFonts use Label.font as-is.

review.reason: UiFonts scales LaF font again and AppIcons passes app-scaled dimensions into FlatSVGIcon. Latent double-scaling integration risk; no physical mixed-DPI reproduction. Public FlatLaf zoom API verified locally.

originalClaim.observed: getAutoScaleFactor() returns 1.0 for a 2560x1599 or 2560x1440 panel and jumps to 1.6 at exactly 1600px. originalClaim.fixIdea: Compute dpi/96 from Xft.dpi (xrdb/XSETTINGS) or Toolkit.getScreenResolution(), round to the nearest 0.25, and feed it to flatlaf.uiScale.

review.reason: Same fallback heuristic. Reject the blanket OS-scale-ignorance wording; source explicitly tests Java2D device transform.

originalClaim.surface: All dialogs: Preferences pages, Project Options, colour chooser, file choosers, hotkey editor, window title bars
originalClaim.observed:
At interface scale 1.6, labels render at about 22 px but checkboxes and radios are about 12-13 px, with no gap to their label ("◉Plain template"). Also unscaled:
- the zoom slider thumb (about 10 px) and its ticks

- the hotkey ✓/✗ buttons (18x18)

Keyboard focus on a checkbox is shown only by a thin outline around the 12 px box.
originalClaim.expected: Every control, icon, inset, gap and hit target scales with the same factor as the text, as FlatLaf does when its UI scale is set.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:1161 eventDispatched() is a global AWT ContainerListener. It calls AppPreferences.setScaledFonts / getScaledFont (prefs/AppPreferences.java:390-452, FONT_SIZE=14 at :520) on every component added, which forces the font to 14*SCALE_FACTOR. FlatLaf's own UIScale is never set: there is no flatlaf.uiScale anywhere in the source. FlatLaf therefore paints icons, borders, insets, arrows and title panes at 1.0. Hard-coded pixel sizes add to it, e.g. JHotkeyInput.java:113,152-154.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Set System.setProperty("flatlaf.uiScale", SCALE_FACTOR) before Theme.install() / LAF setup, or UIManager "defaultFont" plus FlatLaf UIScale. Then delete the Startup ContainerListener font hack and the ad-hoc getScaledFont calls, so FlatLaf scales fonts, icons, insets and hit targets together. This is the same root cause as the unreadable palette captions.

findings.title: Hotkey capture: Escape throws 'Must contain the Ctrl key' and then closes Preferences, leaving the binding blank

originalClaim.title: Hotkey capture: Escape throws 'Must contain the Ctrl key' and then closes Preferences, leaving the binding blank
originalClaim.surface: Preferences > Hotkey settings
originalClaim.observed:
1. Click a binding. The field clears and shows a caret plus tiny ✓ and ✗ icons, with no 'press keys' hint.
2. Press Ctrl+Shift+E. A modal error, parented to null, says 'This key conflicts with: Export file'; the menu calls that action 'Export project bundle…'.
3. Dismiss it and press Escape. Another modal says 'Must contain the Ctrl key'.
4. Dismiss that. The whole Preferences window is gone.
5. Reopen it. The Auto-Propagate field is still blank, stuck in edit mode.
Also, after this close, Ctrl+, did nothing until the canvas was clicked: focus is not returned to the main window.
originalClaim.expected: Escape cancels the capture only. Conflicts and invalid combos are shown inline under the field, with an option to reassign. Nothing closes the dialog mid-edit. Focus returns to the main window when Preferences closes.
originalClaim.rootCause: util/JHotkeyInput.java:289-328 keyPressed treats every key, Escape included, as a candidate binding and calls OptionPane.showMessageDialog(null, …). The unconsumed Escape then reaches the Dialogs.installEscapeToClose binding installed by LFrame.Dialog (gui/generic/LFrame.java:85), which disposes the window once the modal returns. The conflict label uses a different action name than the menu.
originalClaim.fixIdea: In JHotkeyInput, handle VK_ESCAPE as cancel and consume it. Show validation as inline error text or a red border under the field, not a modal. Reuse the menu item's label for conflict messages. Request focus back to the owner frame when the Preferences window closes.

corroborations.title: Circuit list loses its listener to garbage collection and becomes stale
corroborations.verification: Fresh live GC, tab-switch and F2 rename; source establishes lifetime defect.
corroborations.observed: After jcmd GC.run on the private JVM, main is active while inv remains selected in the list. Renaming osc to osc_qa updates the tab and title while the list still displays osc.
reproduction: Open main and inv from the list.
Allow GC or request GC only on a disposable QA JVM.
Click main tab and compare list highlight.
Select osc, press F2, rename to osc_qa; compare row and tab.
corroborations.rootCause: MyListener is a constructor-local variable registered with weak project/library event sources. CircuitListView does not retain it strongly.
corroborations.fix: Retain the listener in a field for the view lifetime, unregister on disposal, and keep current-circuit selection and library mutations synchronized. Guard actions against targets no longer in the project.
corroborations.acceptance: After forced GC, add/rename/delete/reorder/set-main and tab switching update the list immediately. Undo/redo does the same. A deleted row cannot be reopened as a ghost.
corroborations.reason: Unifies add/rename, stale highlight, and recovered deleted-row symptoms. No data-loss claim: ghost editing/saving was not retested.

findings.title: Preferences organisation and wording carried over from old Logisim, with duplicates and misleading names

'Interface scale' shown as a percentage with a 'Restart now' button. Consistent sentence case. Remember the last page. A clean window title ('main — sample' plus a dirty dot).
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/prefs/PreferencesFrame.java:49-60 tab order and :104 showPage(intlIndex). gui/prefs/LayoutOptions.java:40 and WindowOptions.java:78 both use S.getter("layoutAntiAliasing") for AntiAliassing and UI_ANTIALIASING. WindowOptions.java:107-123 zoom slider plus 'windowToolbarImportant' text; :136-143 hard-coded editor theme names. gui/main/Frame.java:655-674 builds the title with Main.DIRTY_MARKER, the [UNSAVED] text and ' (ID:%s, BUILT:%s)' for non-stable builds.

originalClaim.observed: I dragged the divider from x=2269, 2271, 2272, 2275 and 2277 by 200–370 px, slowly and quickly. The panel width did not change, neither during the drag nor after release. originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/ShellLayout.java SizedSplit.doLayout() (~lines 198-214) re-applies the stored size on every layout pass, and continuousLayout=true lays out on each drag step. DIVIDER_SIZE=5 at ShellLayout.java:31 is unscaled.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Track the drag with a PropertyChangeListener on DIVIDER_LOCATION_PROPERTY while the user is dragging (or set an 'adjustingByUser' flag on mousePressed) and update the stored size continuously; only enforce the stored size on window resize. Scale the divider size and give it a hover/drag highlight.

originalClaim.surface: Properties table with more rows than fit (e.g. 64-bit splitter), any row under the pointer
originalClaim.observed: With a 64-row splitter table, 5 wheel notches over the label column did not scroll at all. 3 notches over the value column of 'Bit 10' changed it from 'Output 0' to 'Output 3' with no focus, click or confirmation. Wheeling over Facing rotates the component on the canvas notch by notch. Anyone trying to scroll the list with the wheel will corrupt their circuit.
originalClaim.expected: The wheel always scrolls the panel. Value nudging, if kept at all, only happens on a focused or hovered numeric spinner, or with a modifier (Ctrl/Alt+wheel), and never on dropdowns.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/generic/AttrTable.java:98 table.addMouseWheelListener(this::handleMouseWheel). A MouseWheelListener on the JTable makes Swing deliver wheel events to the table instead of the enclosing JScrollPane, so scrolling dies everywhere. handleMouseWheel (:135-181) then applies values for any editable row under the pointer.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Remove the table-level wheel listener. Implement nudging inside the numeric editor (spinner) when it has focus, or require a modifier and re-dispatch unmodified events to the parent scroll pane (parent.dispatchEvent(SwingUtilities.convertMouseEvent(...))). Never step dropdowns with the wheel.

findings.title: Wheel gestures behave inconsistently: dropdown rows record one undo step per notch, and wheel direction is inverted between row types

originalClaim.title: Wheel gestures behave inconsistently: dropdown rows record one undo step per notch, and wheel direction is inverted between row types
originalClaim.surface: Wheel over Facing / Gate Size / Pen Width (dropdowns) vs Data Bits / numbers
originalClaim.observed: 2 notches over Facing produced 2 separate 'Change Selection Property' undo entries (the undo history grew from 4 to 6 after Gate Size + Facing gestures). Numeric rows coalesce into one entry, but the code comment claims all wheel gestures do. Direction: wheel-up raised Data Bits (8→12), but wheel-up on Pen Width (1) did nothing and wheel-down raised it to 4. Wheel-up on Facing moved East→South→North (up the list). A 6-notch gesture on Data Bits advanced only 5.
originalClaim.expected: One wheel gesture = one undo step for every row type. The same wheel direction always means 'increase / next'.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/generic/AttrTable.java:153-163: the non-editable JComboBox branch calls applyValue immediately on every notch (no pending/settle timer) and uses newIdx = currentIdx + rotation. gui/generic/AttrWheelNudge.java:58 uses next = current - signum(clicks), the opposite sign. AttrTable.java:153 also builds a fresh editor (row.getEditor) on every wheel event.
originalClaim.fixIdea: If wheel editing survives inspector-05, route both paths through the same pending/settle commit and the same sign convention, and coalesce into one undoable action.

review.title: Wheel gestures behave inconsistently: dropdown rows record one undo step per notch, and wheel direction is inverted between row types
review.reason: Option-combo branch immediately applies each notch, numeric branch uses pending settle timer. Throttle ignores close events. Exact lost-notch count and pen-width direction were not independently replayed.

findings.title: Validation happens after the fact in modal dialogs; invalid input is thrown away and messages are inconsistent

originalClaim.title: Validation happens after the fact in modal dialogs; invalid input is thrown away and messages are inconsistent
originalClaim.surface: Label, Circuit Name, Number of Inputs, Connected bus editors
originalClaim.observed:

- A duplicate label gives another 'Message' dialog.
- An out-of-range number gives 'Value Invalid' with a warning icon.
- A non-number gives the raw Java exception text 'For input string: "abc".'
- The RISC-V 'Connected bus' row, whose value reads 'Click to sel...', opens a modal with an ERROR icon just to say no bus exists.
Four different dialog styles for one concept, and none point at the field.
originalClaim.expected: Validate inline: a red outline on the field and a one-line message under the row as the user types, with the text kept so it can be fixed. Commit is blocked until the value is valid, and valid ranges show as placeholder or helper text. Non-actionable states ('no SoC bus in circuit') appear as a disabled dropdown with helper text, not a modal.
originalClaim.rootCause: util/SyntaxChecker.java:84 OptionPane.showMessageDialog(null, ...) (null parent, default INFORMATION type). instance/InstanceComponent.java:139-146: set-then-revert inside attributeValueChanged, plus more null-parent dialogs. gui/generic/AttributeSetTableModel.java:270-278 appends e.toString()/e.getMessage() of ClassCast/NumberFormatException. gui/generic/AttrTable.java:201-210, :486-509, :684-695 show a modal for every AttrTableSetException.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Give Attribute a validate(String) → Optional<String> error hook. Have the cell editor render an inline error state (FlatLaf 'JComponent.outline'='error' plus a message row) and refuse to stop editing while invalid. Map parse failures to human messages ('Enter a whole number from 2 to 64'). Remove the set-then-revert pattern.

review.title: Validation happens after the fact in modal dialogs; invalid input is thrown away and messages are inconsistent
review.reason: AttributeSetTableModel exposes NumberFormatException messages; AttrTable shows modal warnings. Broad claim that every invalid field discards drafts or has the same icon was not live verified.

findings.title: On a fresh window, clicking components shows a completely blank Properties panel (Poke tool is the default), with no empty state; files without a toolbar have no visible Select tool at all

originalClaim.title: On a fresh window, clicking components shows a completely blank Properties panel (Poke tool is the default), with no empty state; files without a toolbar have no visible Select tool at all
originalClaim.surface: Properties panel right after opening any project
originalClaim.observed: The app starts with the Poke (hand) tool active. Clicking the empty canvas or any component (AND gate, 7400 chip, RISC-V) leaves the panel as an empty dark box headed 'PROPERTIES', with no text explaining why. For soc.circ and painters.circ, which have no <toolbar> section, the drawing toolbar is completely empty, so there is not even a visible Select tool to switch to. I had to use Ctrl+A or the right-click 'Show Properties' to see anything.
originalClaim.expected: Clicking a component always selects it and shows its properties, whatever the default tool (the Poke tool could still toggle inputs and also select). When there is really nothing to show, the panel has an empty state ('Select a component to see its properties' plus circuit properties). The core tools (Select/Poke/Wire/Text) are always present regardless of the per-file toolbar.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Frame.java:390 project.setTool(getToolbarData().getFirstTool()), and Poke is first in the default toolbar. The Poke tool has no attribute set, so Frame.viewAttributes sets a null model. gui/generic/AttrTable.java:309-335 NullAttrModel renders nothing, and Frame.inspectorTitle falls back to 'Properties'. The per-file toolbar (file/XmlReader toolbar data) fully controls whether Select exists.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Start in the Select tool, or make a Poke-click also select the component for the inspector. Add an empty-state component to AttrTable. Always prepend the base tools to the toolbar independent of the project file.

review.title: On a fresh window, clicking components shows a completely blank Properties panel (Poke tool is the default), with no empty state; files without a toolbar have no visible Select tool at all
review.reason: Fresh window has active Poke tool and a blank bordered Properties panel without guidance. Missing Select tool in files with custom/empty toolbars was not independently tested.

findings.title: Closing the Properties panel is a one-way trip: no menu item or shortcut brings it back, 'Show Properties' does nothing, and the hidden state persists across restarts

Frame.java:1182-1188 viewComponentAttributes only swaps the model. LayoutPrefs.java:127 persists the hidden state.

findings.title: The inspector is still the 2005 raw two-column JTable: no groups, no search, no descriptions, no editor affordances, booleans as Yes/No dropdowns

originalClaim.title: The inspector is still the 2005 raw two-column JTable: no groups, no search, no descriptions, no editor affordances, booleans as Yes/No dropdowns
originalClaim.surface: Properties table for every component
originalClaim.observed:
- A flat list of rows in declaration order, with no header and no grouping (no General / Appearance / Label / Simulation / HDL sections).
- No filter field. Hovering a label shows no description of what the property does (e.g. what 'Output Value 0/1' or 'Behavior Simple' mean).
- No row hover highlight.
- Values are plain text with no hint which are dropdowns, text fields or dialogs: chevrons and field outlines appear only after clicking.
- Booleans ('Negate 1', 'Label Visible', 'Use fixed box') are Yes/No dropdowns needing two clicks.
- Numbers (Number of Inputs) are bare text fields with no spinner and no range hint.
- Read-only rows (wire Direction/Length) look exactly like editable ones, and clicking them gives no feedback.
- The user can recognise the old Logisim attribute table immediately.
originalClaim.expected:
A modern property grid:
- Collapsible group headers, and a search/filter box at the top.
- Label tooltips with descriptions.
- Row hover.
- Checkboxes or switches for booleans, spinners with min/max for numbers, visible chevrons on dropdowns.
- Read-only values dimmed or shown as plain info rows.
- Rows for the label, font and colour of the label grouped together.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/generic/AttrTable.java:80-110: a plain JTable with a single HdlColorRenderer for all cells and no header or grouping. Editors come from Attribute.getCellEditor (data/Attributes.java), where booleans are option combos. AttrTable.java:296-307 only produces tooltips for elided text. Attributes carry no group or description metadata.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Replace AttrTable with a property-sheet component: add optional group + description metadata to Attribute (defaulting by StdAttr kind), render headers as collapsible rows, add a filter field, and use type-specific renderers/editors (JCheckBox for BooleanAttribute, JSpinner for IntegerRange/BitWidth, combo with a visible arrow).

review.title: The inspector is still the 2005 raw two-column JTable: no groups, no search, no descriptions, no editor affordances, booleans as Yes/No dropdowns
review.reason: Live table lacks persistent editor affordances and grouping. Sections, search and property help are improvements; a two-column table itself is not a bug.

findings.title: Cells have no padding: text is flush to the cell edges and labels run into values ('Output Value0/1', 'Circuit Namemain')

originalClaim.title: Cells have no padding: text is flush to the cell edges and labels run into values ('Output Value0/1', 'Circuit Namemain')
originalClaim.surface: All Properties rows

The row rhythm (32 px rows for ~20 px text) is tight, and dropdown popup items (~35 px) are taller than the rows.

review.title: Cells have no padding: text is flush to the cell edges and labels run into values ('Output Value0/1', 'Circuit Namemain')

findings.title: Heavy selection and focus styling: saturated full-width blue row bars and a blue rectangle around the whole table

originalClaim.title: Heavy selection and focus styling: saturated full-width blue row bars and a blue rectangle around the whole table
originalClaim.surface: Properties table when a row is clicked or edited
originalClaim.observed: Clicking a value paints the label cell in saturated accent blue with dark text, while the value cell becomes a boxed editor. After Enter, or after a dialog, the next row gets a full-width bright blue bar that stays there. A 1–2 px blue focus rectangle surrounds the entire table whenever it has focus. Multi-row selection (Ctrl+click) looks like the same heavy bars. The panel looks 'selected' most of the time.

originalClaim.rootCause: fpga/gui/HdlColorRenderer.java:74-77 applies Table.selectionBackground to any selected cell, and the table uses row selection. The FlatLaf focus border is on the JScrollPane created at gui/generic/AttrTable.java:101.

review.title: Heavy selection and focus styling: saturated full-width blue row bars and a blue rectangle around the whole table
review.reason: Strong blue row/focus styling is visible during multi-edit, but heaviness is aesthetic. Retain visible keyboard focus while improving contrast and restraint.

findings.title: Panel title uppercases everything (misrepresenting case-sensitive names), shows raw coordinates, truncates, and says 'VARIOUS ITEMS × 3'

review.title: Panel title uppercases everything (misrepresenting case-sensitive names), shows raw coordinates, truncates, and says 'VARIOUS ITEMS × 3'

findings.title: In the Appearance editor the panel header is stale: it keeps the last layout selection ('LED (1170,970)') while showing circuit or shape attributes

findings.title: Any selection that includes a wire loses every shared property: rubber-band selecting pins + gates shows only the FPGA row

originalClaim.title: Any selection that includes a wire loses every shared property: rubber-band selecting pins + gates shows only the FPGA row
originalClaim.surface: Properties for multi-selection made by dragging a rectangle

AttrTableSelectionModel.getTitle already excludes wires from the count.

review.title: Any selection that includes a wire loses every shared property: rubber-band selecting pins + gates shows only the FPGA row
review.reason: Source confirms intersection includes wire attributes. This is mathematically correct for all selected objects, but component-only aggregate editing may be more useful. Define scope explicitly before excluding wires; do not silently pretend a change applied to everything.

findings.title: Multi-select editing: '(various)' looks like a real value, the editor pre-fills the first item's value, and labels are silently auto-numbered

originalClaim.title: Multi-select editing: '(various)' looks like a real value, the editor pre-fills the first item's value, and labels are silently auto-numbered

review.title: Multi-select editing: '(various)' looks like a real value, the editor pre-fills the first item's value, and labels are silently auto-numbered

findings.title: Editing several table rows at once creates three undo entries, including an empty one

originalClaim.title: Editing several table rows at once creates three undo entries, including an empty one

review.title: Editing several table rows at once creates three undo entries, including an empty one

findings.title: Property naming is inconsistent: Title Case vs sentence case, trailing colons, Java font names, instruction text as a value
