findings.title: Every tile caption is clipped: unreadable at 1.6, invisible at 2.0, cut short at 1.0

originalClaim.title: Every tile caption is clipped: unreadable at 1.6, invisible at 2.0, cut short at 1.0
originalClaim.surface: Component palette tiles in every group, including Pinned and Recently used
originalClaim.observed: At scale 1.6 only the top ~40% of each caption shows ("NOT", "Buffer", "AND" are a row of cut-off glyph tops), and names are also shortened to about 4-5 characters ("Split", "Tun", "Prior", "CD…" for CDMUX). At 2.0 the captions are gone entirely and the 40 px icons nearly fill the tile. At 1.0 the captions can be read but are cut short: "Controlle...", "Pull Resis...", "Demultipl...", "Exponent...", "7418: dua...". The selected tile's accent-coloured caption is clipped too.
originalClaim.expected: Tile size, preview area and text position scale with the interface scale. Each tile shows a full, legible name (two lines if needed, or a short name), with a comfortable gap under the icon.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentTile.java:44-50 fixes PREVIEW_HEIGHT=40, WIDTH=68, HEIGHT=62 in device pixels (applied at :67-69). The caption is drawn at PREVIEW_HEIGHT + Spacing.sm() + ascent - 2 (:185-188) with UiFonts.small(), which is scaled. At 1.6 that is ~40+13+18 = 71 px, below the 62 px tile. The width left for the caption is 68-2*xs = 56 px (:184).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Pass every tile constant through UiScale.scaled(), or better, lay the caption out with FontMetrics (preview = scaled BOX_SIZE + padding; height = preview + 2 lines of small font + padding). Let tiles grow to share the available width (see palette-18), allow two-line captions with a word-wrap ellipsis, and add a short display name per component ("FP Add", "7400 · 4×NAND"). Add a screenshot test at 1.0, 1.6 and 2.0 that fails if a caption's bottom is past the tile's bottom.

review.reason: Live native crops show chopped captions at 1.6 and absent captions at 2.0. One geometry defect, not one bug per tile.

findings.title: Dozens of tiles look identical, so the palette can't be scanned even with readable names

originalClaim.title: Dozens of tiles look identical, so the palette can't be scanned even with readable names
originalClaim.surface: Arithmetic (float units), Chips & TTL, Advanced, and the project-circuit group
originalClaim.observed: The 18 floating-point tiles reuse the integer icons (+, -, ×, ÷, √, abs, min/max), so Adder and Floating Point Adder look the same; at 1.0 all 18 are captioned "Floating ...". The 63 TTL tiles share one black chip icon and differ only in a clipped number. All 26 of PC.circ's subcircuits (CAnd, COR, MUX, MUX, DMUX…, ALU, CPU) share one white chip icon. TCL REDS console and TCL generic share an icon, as do Binary-to-BCD and BCD-to-7-segment (green PLA chip) and Pico and Nios ("uP").
originalClaim.expected: Every tile can be told apart at a glance: a distinct icon or badge (for example an "FP" corner badge), a short subtitle for TTL chips ("7400 · 4×NAND"), and user subcircuits drawn from their actual appearance with their full name.
originalClaim.rootCause: ToolPreviewIcon.java:96 draws tool.paintIcon(), and each factory brings its own legacy icon. AbstractTtlGate.java:103 uses setIconName("ttl.gif") for every chip. Float factories reuse ArithmeticIcon; subcircuits use the generic subcirc icon. Component names are long library strings (std.properties:75-184 "Floating Point …", :1014 "7418: dual 4-input NAND gate…").
originalClaim.fixIdea: For subcircuits, render a small preview of the circuit's appearance (SubcircuitFactory has the appearance) instead of the generic icon. Give FP tiles a badge and TTL tiles a two-line caption (number plus function). Add a short palette name for each component to the strings files, separate from the long description used in tooltips.

review.reason: Recovered 1.0 crop visibly repeats Floating... labels; icons often indicate the operation but fail to distinguish integer from FP variants. Exact counts and all subcircuits were not re-counted.

findings.title: "Show the library tree" opens the untouched 2005 Logisim JTree, broken at scale

originalClaim.title: "Show the library tree" opens the untouched 2005 Logisim JTree, broken at scale
originalClaim.surface: Palette header folder button → library tree view
originalClaim.observed: The tree view is the old Logisim explorer: bold labels, folder icons, a chip-with-magnifier icon for the current circuit, and an old-style "main ●" marker. At 1.6 the row height is shorter than the scaled bold font, so descenders are cut ("Wiring", "mega", "Floating"). Names are truncated at the panel edge ("Floating Point Arit", "BFH mega functior", "Input/Output Extr") and a horizontal scrollbar appears. At 2.0 the rows overlap, the chevrons stay tiny, and the "main" and "BALDUR" icons overlap each other.
originalClaim.expected: If the tree must stay (it is the only place to unload or reorder libraries), restyle it like the rest of the shell: regular-weight text, row height taken from the font, scaled chevrons and SVG icons, no horizontal scroll, and ellipsis truncation with tooltips. Better, move library management into a dialog or a context menu on the palette section headers and drop the second view.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/generic/ProjectExplorer.java:289-291: the cell renderer sets AppPreferences.getScaledFont() (FONT_SIZE × scale) but the JTree's row height is never updated (no setRowHeight). Bold comes from the renderer's default font and deriveFont(BOLD) at :290/:313. Icons come from ToolIcon/legacy paint code (:523-602 uses BOX_SIZE with fixed offsets). The tree is embedded in gui/main/Toolbox.java:54-60.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Set tree.setRowHeight(0) (let the renderer decide) or font height + scaled padding; drop bold except for the current circuit; replace ProjectExplorer's ToolIcon/folder glyphs with AppIcons; hide the horizontal scrollbar and ellipsize. Long term, replace the tree with section-header context menus in the palette (Unload / Reload / Move up).

review.reason: Tree fallback clips/overlaps scaled text; source has fixed LaF rows and scaled icons/fonts. Styling age is not the failure criterion.

findings.title: The project's own subcircuits are buried at the very bottom, under an uppercased file name

originalClaim.title: The project's own subcircuits are buried at the very bottom, under an uppercased file name
originalClaim.surface: Palette: group for the current project's circuits ("PC", "SAMPLE")
originalClaim.observed: In PC.circ, the user's 26 subcircuits sit below Logic, Wiring, Arithmetic (31 tiles), Memory, I/O (23), Displays, Chips & TTL (63) and Advanced. Getting to them takes about 80 wheel notches. The heading is the file name uppercased ("PC", "SAMPLE"). They are the parts a student uses most in a multi-circuit project.
originalClaim.expected: A "This project" / "Circuits" group at the top, right after Pinned and Recent, with the real circuit names and appearance previews. Library groups for loaded .circ/.jar libraries come next, and TTL and Advanced are collapsed by default.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentPalette.java:190-205: the grouped LinkedHashMap is seeded with PaletteCatalog.Group.values() first, and anything PaletteCatalog.groupOf() does not know (the project file itself, loaded libraries) is added later with computeIfAbsent, so it lands after ADVANCED. SectionPanel.setTitle uppercases it (SectionPanel.java:114).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Handle the project root library (collectFrom with projectRoot=true) as its own group titled "This project", inserted right after Recent. Collapse CHIPS and ADVANCED by default. Don't uppercase user-supplied names.

review.reason: Unknown/project libraries are appended after preseeded built-in categories. Exact wheel-notch count was not retested.

findings.title: Search is a plain substring match on the display name: no abbreviations, noisy matches, no ranking, no empty state

originalClaim.title: Search is a plain substring match on the display name: no abbreviations, noisy matches, no ranking, no empty state
originalClaim.surface: Palette search field
originalClaim.observed: "mux" returns nothing, even though Find Action (double Shift) finds Multiplexer for the same query. In PC.circ "mux" only finds the user's own circuits. "and" returns AND and NAND plus Minimum and Maximum, Random, 18 TTL chips and a SoC tile. "pla" also matches 7-Segment Display and Hex Digit Display. "output" never offers an output Pin. "gate" lists the whole TTL range. A German word returns nothing. A query with no results ("xyzzy") leaves a completely blank panel with no message. Results are grouped by category rather than ranked, so the exact match is not first, and matched text is not highlighted.
originalClaim.expected: Rank results by quality: exact, then prefix, then word start, then fuzzy. Also match aliases (mux, demux, ff, dff, reg, led, 7seg, pin in/out), descriptions and the English name when the UI is localized. Show a flat ranked list while searching, with the match highlighted. For no results, show "No components match 'xyzzy'" and a hint.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentPalette.java:162-166 matches() is name.toLowerCase().contains(filterText) on getDisplayName() only. rebuild() (:185-207) keeps the category grouping while filtering, and addGroup returns early for empty groups (:223), so zero results leave nothing to show. OmniSearchDialog (gui/search) uses a separate fuzzy matcher, so the two searches disagree.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Extract one matcher (reuse the Find Action scorer), add an alias table next to PaletteCatalog, and search name + aliases + description + English name. While filtering, show one ranked "Results" group with highlighted matches, and add an empty-state label. Enter already takes the first result (:262-264); with ranking it will take the best one.

review.reason: Live mux query returns an empty palette without explanation. Substring-only matching is confirmed. Cross-language matching is a proposal, not an existing promise.

findings.title: The side panel can't be widened by dragging, and its width and divider are fixed pixels

originalClaim.title: The side panel can't be widened by dragging, and its width and divider are fixed pixels
originalClaim.surface: Divider between palette and canvas (also between canvas and inspector)
originalClaim.observed: Dragging the 5 px divider at x=330-334 (native) and the inspector divider at x=2265-2269 changed nothing, and shell.sideWidth stayed at 260 in preferences. A control drag on the canvas moved a component normally, so the input works. The divider is the same colour as the panel, so it is invisible. The panel is 260 device px at every scale: about 162 logical px at 1.6, and only 2 tile columns at 2.0. With the width forced to 600 through preferences the grid reflows to 7 columns, but the captions stay clipped because tiles never grow.
originalClaim.expected: A visible (on hover) divider with a scaled hit area that drags smoothly and remembers the width. Default and minimum widths scale with the interface scale.
originalClaim.rootCause: Likely cause: gui/shell/ShellLayout.java:201-214 SizedSplit.doLayout() re-applies the stored size on every layout. With setContinuousLayout(true) (:120), each drag step triggers a layout that snaps the divider back. The stored size is only updated in the divider's mouseReleased (:170-178), which then reads the already-reset location. DIVIDER_SIZE = 5 (:31) and LayoutPrefs.MIN_PANEL=160 / DEFAULT_SIDE_WIDTH=260 (LayoutPrefs.java:26,40) are unscaled.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Skip enforcement while the divider is being dragged (set a flag in mousePressed, clear it in mouseReleased), or listen to DIVIDER_LOCATION_PROPERTY with the adjusting guard that already exists. Store logical widths and multiply by UiScale. Scale DIVIDER_SIZE and paint a hover or drag highlight.

review.reason: One live 2.0 divider drag did not widen the panel; doLayout restores the stored location before release saves it. This fresh session used a 320px migrated side width, not the report's universal 260px claim.

findings.title: Keyboard use is minimal: no arrow keys, a Tab stop per tile, focus scrolls off-screen

originalClaim.title: Keyboard use is minimal: no arrow keys, a Tab stop per tile, focus scrolls off-screen
originalClaim.surface: Palette tiles and section headers
originalClaim.observed: Down from the search field focuses the first tile, but Right/Left/Up/Down do nothing inside the grid. Tab visits every tile one at a time (about 250 stops before leaving the palette). After 55 Tabs the focus ring was below the viewport and the palette had not scrolled. Enter then armed D Flip-Flop, a tile the user couldn't see. Section headers can't be focused, so groups can't be folded from the keyboard. There is no keyboard route to the tile menu (Shift+F10 / Menu key), no type-ahead, no Home/End, and no shortcut that focuses the search field.
originalClaim.expected: The grid behaves as one focus stop with arrow-key navigation (roving tabindex), Home/End and PageUp/Down. The focused tile is scrolled into view. Headers are focusable and toggle with Space/Enter or Left/Right. Shift+F10 opens the tile menu. A shortcut (for example Ctrl+Shift+F or "/") focuses the search field, and Up from the first row returns to it.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentTile.java:70 setFocusable(true) on every tile, and the key listener (:98-107) handles only ENTER/SPACE. The focusGained handler (:109-120) only repaints, with no scrollRectToVisible. SectionPanel.java:53-67 has only a mouseClicked listener on a non-focusable JPanel. ComponentPalette.java:266-269 focusFirstTile() is the only way in.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Add a grid-navigation handler in ComponentPalette that knows the tile order and column count (from WrapLayout), moves focus with arrows and calls scrollRectToVisible on focus. Make one tile per grid focusable (roving). Make the SectionPanel header a focusable button-like component. Bind Shift+F10/CONTEXT_MENU to showTileMenu.

review.reason: Tile keys only handle Enter/Space and focusGained only repaints; sections are mouse-only. Live Down/Right left focus on the first tile. The 35-Tab capture still had a visible focused tile and does not prove the report's offscreen claim.

findings.title: Old Logisim bitmap icons sit beside the new line icons, and some vanish on the dark background

originalClaim.title: Old Logisim bitmap icons sit beside the new line icons, and some vanish on the dark background
originalClaim.surface: Palette tiles, mostly Input & output, Displays, Wiring & routing, Chips & TTL, Advanced
originalClaim.observed: The line-drawn gate icons are next to the original coloured 16 px Logisim icons: blue Button "B", blue DIP switch, red/blue joystick, keyboard "K" with a black drop shadow, teal serial port, "Local Bus" bitmap, telnet computers, red/white POR, red LED, green/grey LED bar, RGB swatches, blue "Hel" TTY, green-dot LED matrix, the green PLA chip, the red X "Do not connect", the green splitter and the green pull resistor. Black outlines and bodies disappear on #1E1F22: the TTL chip, the joystick stick, the dot-matrix square and the keyboard shadow. Sizes are inconsistent: Constant is a tiny "1•" and Pin is much smaller than its neighbours.
originalClaim.expected: One icon family: monochrome SVG line icons at a consistent optical size, drawn in the theme's foreground, with at most a single accent colour.
originalClaim.rootCause: 21 classes in gui/icons/ hard-code colours: JoystickIcon.java:22-44 uses Color.BLUE, RED and BLACK, and KeyboardIcon.java:27-41 uses LIGHT_GRAY, BLACK and WHITE; the others include LedIcon, SevenSegmentIcon, DipSwitchIcon, ButtonIcon, TtyIcon, LedMatrixIcon and ArithmeticIcon. 13 factories still load GIF/PNG files through InstanceFactory.setIconName (ttl.gif, tunnel.gif, probe.gif, por.png, pla.gif, noconnect.gif, localbus.gif, telnet.gif, realtimeclock.gif, extender.gif, pio.gif, displaydecoder.gif, programmablegenerator.gif), and those are painted at a fixed x+2 offset (InstanceFactory.java:295).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Commission an SVG set for all palette components and route them through AppIcons (FlatSVGIcon with a colour filter bound to Tokens.foreground/accent). Retire the gui/icons Java2D classes and the GIFs. Until then, pass the palette's foreground colour to BaseIcon subclasses instead of Color.BLACK.

review.reason: Live crops show white-backed raster icons and colored legacy marks alongside monochrome symbols; visibility varies. Not all claimed icon classes were individually verified.

findings.title: Recently used lags behind, duplicates pinned items, and the selection shows in two places

originalClaim.title: Recently used lags behind, duplicates pinned items, and the selection shows in two places
originalClaim.surface: Pinned and Recently used groups
originalClaim.observed: Picking NOT didn't add it to Recently used. It only appeared after something else rebuilt the palette (placing a part), and clicking a recent item doesn't move it to the front. Pinned AND showed three times with a star (Pinned, Recently used and Logic). The selected tool is highlighted in every group that contains it (NOT in both Recent and Logic). The Pinned group doesn't exist until something is pinned, so the feature can't be discovered. Pinning makes all the content below jump by one group height.
originalClaim.expected: Recent updates immediately (or when the part is placed) and leaves out pinned items. Only the tile the user clicked shows as selected, or all copies clearly as the same selection. An empty Pinned group shows a one-line hint ("Right-click a part to pin it"), and the scroll position stays anchored when groups change.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentPalette.java:272-279 choose() updates the recents list and preference but never rebuilds the Recent group. :186-187 builds Pinned and Recent from independent lists (no exclusion). :285-289 setCurrentTool() marks every tile whose tool == current. :223 skips empty groups.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Rebuild only the Recent group when the part is placed (on ACTION_SET_TOOL after placement) and filter out pinned keys. Track the tile that was actually clicked for the selection highlight. Always render Pinned, with an empty-state hint. Save and restore the scroll anchor (the first visible tile) in rebuild().

review.reason: choose() mutates/persists recents without rebuilding; pin/recent/category independently render the same tool. Multiple highlights are consistent identity indicators, not multiple selections.

findings.title: The tile menu has one item, covers the tile, and a subcircuit tile can't open its circuit

originalClaim.title: The tile menu has one item, covers the tile, and a subcircuit tile can't open its circuit
originalClaim.surface: Right-click menu on a tile; double-clicking a subcircuit tile
originalClaim.observed: Right-clicking any tile gives a menu with a single item, "Pin to top" or "Remove from pinned". It has no icon and opens at the tile's centre, covering the tile. Double-clicking the BALDUR subcircuit tile only arms it; there's no way to open or edit a subcircuit from the palette. There's also no "Show help", "Place at centre", "Edit appearance" or "Reveal in library".
originalClaim.expected: A menu opened at the pointer, with Pin/Unpin (star icon), Help for this component, and for subcircuits: Edit circuit, Edit appearance and Rename. Double-clicking a subcircuit opens it, as double-clicking in the old tree did.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentPalette.java:247-259 showTileMenu builds a one-item JPopupMenu and calls menu.show(tile, w/2, h/2). ComponentTile.java:88-95 handles only mousePressed (choose or context menu), with no click-count check.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Pass the MouseEvent point to showTileMenu. Reuse the circuit actions from the Circuits view / ToolboxManip for SubcircuitFactory tools. Handle clickCount==2 on subcircuit tiles by calling project.setCurrentCircuit().

review.reason: A one-item pin menu and no double-click circuit editor are verified in source, but richer actions need an intentional product decision; use Circuits for editing today.

findings.title: Mixed terminology: "Pin to top" vs the Pin part, Library vs Components, old "Add …" tooltips, two parts both called PLA

originalClaim.title: Mixed terminology: "Pin to top" vs the Pin part, Library vs Components, old "Add …" tooltips, two parts both called PLA
originalClaim.surface: Palette menu, headers, tooltips and names
originalClaim.observed: In a logic simulator where "Pin" is a part, the menu says "Pin to top" and the group is "Pinned" (the code calls them favourites). The panel is "LIBRARY", the field says "Search components", the activity bar tooltip says "Library", and the tree toggle says "library tree". Palette groups ("Wiring & routing", "Chips & TTL") don't match the tree and Find Action names ("Wiring", "Multiplexers", "TTL", "sample › Multiplexers"). Tooltips use the old Logisim wording "Add AND Gate", "Add CDMUX", "Add 7418: dual 4-input NAND gate(Schmitt trigger)" (no space before the parenthesis). The Logic PLA and the I/O PLA ROM are both named "PLA" with the tooltip "Add PLA".
originalClaim.expected: One vocabulary: "Components" for the panel and "Favourites" (star) for pinning. Tooltips give the name, a one-line description and ports/shortcut, never "Add X". Every component has a unique name ("PLA ROM"), and the same group names are used everywhere.
originalClaim.rootCause: resources/.../strings/gui/gui.properties:515-532 (libraryTab, paletteFilterHint, palettePin="Pin to top", paletteGroupFavourites="Pinned"). The tooltip is tools.properties:5 addToolText="Add %s", used by AddTool.java:313 and ComponentTile.describe() (:125-128). std.properties:385 PLA=PLA and :507 PlaRomComponent=PLA; std.properties:1014 is missing a space.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Rename the strings: Favourite/Unfavourite with a star icon, "Components" for the panel title and activity bar. Build a rich tooltip in ComponentTile (bold name, description, library), rename PlaRomComponent to "PLA ROM", fix the TTL description strings, and make the Find Action provider use the palette group names.

review.reason: Two different factories have the identical display label PLA. That ambiguity is actionable; Pin to top and Library terminology are editorial choices.

findings.title: The groups mix essential and exotic parts; there's no output pin, and TTL/Advanced are open by default

originalClaim.title: The groups mix essential and exotic parts; there's no output pin, and TTL/Advanced are open by default
originalClaim.surface: Palette group taxonomy
originalClaim.observed: "Input & output" has 23 tiles mixing the essentials (Pin, Probe, Clock, Constant, Power, Ground) with rarely used peripherals (Joystick, Keyboard, Serial port, Local Bus, Telnet, Real-time clock, Digital oscilloscope, PLA ROM). "Advanced" is a catch-all of TCL consoles, BFH BCD converters, soft CPUs and SoC. "Wiring & routing" combines splitter/tunnel with plexers, transistors and bit extender. The palette has only one "Pin" (input by default), and searching "output" doesn't find it, although the toolbar has separate input and output pins. The 63-tile TTL group and the SoC group are expanded by default.
originalClaim.expected: Pinned, Recent, This project, Basics (Input pin, Output pin, Clock, Constant, Probe, Splitter, Tunnel, Ground/Power), Gates, Plexers, Arithmetic, Memory, Displays, Peripherals, then TTL and SoC collapsed at the bottom. Separate Input pin and Output pin tiles (same factory, preset attribute).
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/PaletteCatalog.java:148-217: BY_LIBRARY maps whole libraries ("input/output-extra" → INPUT_OUTPUT, tcl/bfh-praktika/soc/hdl-ip → ADVANCED), and BY_TOOL moves only 7 wiring tools and 8 I/O tools. ComponentPalette.java:238 opens every group by default.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Extend BY_TOOL into a curated table covering every built-in tool, with a BASICS group and a PERIPHERALS group. Add a per-group default-collapsed flag (TTL, SoC, TCL). Add palette-only "Output pin" and "Input pin" presets that create the Pin factory with the output attribute set.

review.reason: Catalog regrouping, collapsed advanced groups and an output-pin preset are design choices. Output search discoverability belongs to palette-05.

findings.title: Group headers: Pinned/Recent titles indented, no hover or count, low contrast, fold state forgotten

originalClaim.title: Group headers: Pinned/Recent titles indented, no hover or count, low contrast, fold state forgotten
originalClaim.surface: SectionPanel headers in the palette
originalClaim.observed: Pinned and Recently used put their badge icon before the chevron, so their titles start about 20 px right of LOGIC, ARITHMETIC and the other headers. Headers have no hover background or item count and show only a hand cursor. The header and caption text colour #747D8E on #1E1F22 has a contrast ratio of 3.98:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for this small text. A group folded by the user opens again after a relaunch.
originalClaim.expected: Chevron always in the first column, badge after it. A hover background and an item count ("LOGIC 13"). Text at 4.5:1 or better. Fold state saved per group name.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/SectionPanel.java:57-60 adds badgeLabel WEST and the chevron as titleLabel's icon (:118-124). There is no hover or mouseEntered code (:61-67). The colour is Tokens.sidePanelHeaderForeground() (:84; Tokens.java:66) and the captions use Tokens.mutedForeground() (ComponentTile.java:182; Tokens.java:84-85). Fold state is kept in memory only: ComponentPalette.java:70 expanded map.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Put the chevron in its own leading JLabel and the badge between it and the title. Paint a hover fill in SectionPanel and add an optional count. Raise mutedForeground / sidePanelHeaderForeground to about #8C94A3 or lighter in dark theme. Save expanded state in AppPreferences keyed by group id.

review.reason: Collapse state is in-memory only and header has only a click listener; persisting collapse and adding hover/count are separate UX choices. Contrast is consolidated under codeaudit-16.

findings.title: The header's view-toggle icon is a folder, with no hover state and a small target

originalClaim.title: The header's view-toggle icon is a folder, with no hover state and a small target
originalClaim.surface: Palette header button next to "LIBRARY"
originalClaim.observed: A bare folder glyph (about 20 px at 1.6), flush against the right edge, with no hover or pressed background. Its tooltip says "Show the library tree", but a folder normally means open a file. In tree mode it turns into a "list with magnifier" glyph whose meaning is unclear. Nothing shows which view is active.
originalClaim.expected: A proper icon button (hover fill, 28-32 logical px target), or a small segmented control [Grid | Tree] or a view menu ("View as grid / list / tree"). A list view with full names would also fix most of the legibility problem.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Toolbox.java:63-65 setBorderPainted(false) and setContentAreaFilled(false) remove FlatLaf's toolbar-button hover. :83 uses the FOLDER / LIST_FILTER icons at size 14.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Use FlatClientProperties BUTTON_TYPE = toolBarButton (keeps hover and pressed states) and a view-mode dropdown. Add a compact "list" mode (icon + full name per row) as a third view.

review.reason: Folder glyph and no standard button fill are present. Replace with a named two-state view toggle for clarity; working toggle itself is not broken.

findings.title: Search field: placeholder cut off, icon touching the border and text, faint clear button

originalClaim.title: Search field: placeholder cut off, icon touching the border and text, faint clear button
originalClaim.surface: Palette search field
originalClaim.observed: At the default width the placeholder reads "Search compone...", and at 2.0 "Search com...". The magnifier sits about 2 px from the field's left border with no gap before the text. The clear × is small, low-contrast grey and a tiny hit target.
originalClaim.expected: A short placeholder that fits ("Search" or "Filter parts"), a scaled 8 px inset and a 6 px icon gap, and a clear button with a hover state and at least a 24 px target.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/FilterField.java:48-49: the leading JLabel is added without a border or gap. gui.properties paletteFilterHint = "Search components" is too long for the 260 px panel (palette-06).

review.reason: Placeholder truncation at 2.0 and cramped leading icon are visible. At this fresh 320px width the 1.6 placeholder fits, so failure is width-dependent.

findings.title: Dragging a tile onto the canvas does nothing

originalClaim.title: Dragging a tile onto the canvas does nothing
originalClaim.surface: Palette tile → canvas
originalClaim.observed: Pressing on the OR tile and dragging to the canvas arms the OR tool on press. During the drag there is no ghost and no cursor change, and on release nothing is placed; the user has to click the canvas again. Every comparable editor (Figma, Qt Designer, Simulink, Digital) supports drag-to-place.
originalClaim.expected: Drag from a tile shows the component ghost following the pointer and places it where the mouse is released, snapped to the grid. Click-then-click keeps working.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/palette/ComponentTile.java:88-95 only calls onChoose on mousePressed. There is no TransferHandler or DragGestureRecognizer, and the canvas has no drop target.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Add a DragSource on the tile that exports the Tool. On the canvas, a DropTarget calls AddTool's placement logic at the drop point (the ghost comes from AddTool.mouseMoved).

review.reason: Source exposes click-to-arm only; drag-to-place is not implemented. No new live drag-placement test or claim of a promised drag workflow.

findings.title: At scale 2.0 the palette falls apart: 2 columns, clipped star, truncated headers

originalClaim.title: At scale 2.0 the palette falls apart: 2 columns, clipped star, truncated headers
originalClaim.surface: Palette at --scale 2.0

findings.title: Tile states and grid are weak: 1 px focus ring, faint hover, ragged grid, tiny icons at 1.0

findings.title: Found along the way: unnamed autosave files written to $HOME, and a startup prompt for each one

originalClaim.title: Found along the way: unnamed autosave files written to $HOME, and a startup prompt for each one
originalClaim.surface: Startup "Autosave found" dialog
originalClaim.observed: After any abnormal exit, the next launch shows an "Autosave found" dialog for every .logisim-unnamed-autosave_*.circ.autosave file in the home folder. That includes ones from an Untitled project the user never touched: one is created at startup even when a file is opened. The message shows the raw hidden file name. The buttons "Save / Save and load / Discard" don't say what happens, Save is the default button, and closing the dialog leaves the file for next time. Because the files live in $HOME, the parallel QA rigs (and the user's own normal Logisim session) see each other's autosaves, and "Discard" in one instance deletes another's recovery file.
originalClaim.expected: Recovery files in an app data folder (~/.local/share/logisim/autosave), never created for a pristine Untitled project. One "Restore unsaved work?" dialog listing all recoverable projects with timestamps. Recovery tied to the instance that wrote it.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:997-1033 lists System.getProperty("user.home") for the unnamed-autosave prefix, shows one OptionPane per file, and deletes the file on Discard (:1033).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Move autosaves to an app-data folder with a per-instance lock. Skip autosaving an unmodified Untitled project. Merge the prompts into a single restore dialog. For the QA rig now: launch with -Duser.home pointing inside the rig directory.

review.reason: Loader and startup share user.home autosaves and Discard deletes the selected file. Harness interference is confirmed by design, not independently reproduced data loss. This run isolated user.home and never cleared real autosaves.

findings.title: Interface scale only enlarges fonts; every Look-and-Feel metric stays at 1x (checkboxes, radios, sliders, arrows, close buttons, menu shortcuts, icons)

originalClaim.title: Interface scale only enlarges fonts; every Look-and-Feel metric stays at 1x (checkboxes, radios, sliders, arrows, close buttons, menu shortcuts, icons)
originalClaim.surface: Whole app: Preferences, menus, dialogs, tabs, OptionPanes, file chooser
originalClaim.observed: At 1.6 (the user's default) checkbox squares are about 12 px next to 22 px text, with no gap between box and label ('☑Use anti aliasing'). The scale slider thumb is a tiny triangle on a hairline track. At 2.0/2.5, menu shortcut text is about 10 px next to 28–35 px item text, and check marks and submenu arrows are tiny. Other elements that stay at 1x: tab-close ×, dialog close (×) buttons, OptionPane question icon, combo arrows, file-chooser toolbar and file icons (about 12 px), scrollbar widths.
originalClaim.expected: Every control, glyph, inset, row height and icon scales together with the text, as FlatLaf does natively with UIScale.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:1161-1188: a global AWTEventListener re-fonts every JButton/JLabel/JMenuItem/etc. on COMPONENT_ADDED via AppPreferences.getScaledFont (prefs/AppPreferences.java:445-451), which derives every font from the constant FONT_SIZE=14 (:520) × SCALE_FACTOR. FlatLaf's own scale is never set: Main.java:81-114 sets no 'flatlaf.uiScale' and nothing else does. So FlatLaf keeps UIScale=1 for icons, insets, arrow sizes, row heights and accelerator fonts (MenuItem.acceleratorFont is never touched). util/UiScale.java documents this as intentional 'for now'.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Before installing the LaF, set System.setProperty("flatlaf.uiScale", SCALE_FACTOR), or scale 'defaultFont' and let FlatLaf derive everything. Delete the AWT re-font listener and getScaledFont. Route AppPreferences.getScaled/UiScale through com.formdev.flatlaf.util.UIScale. Then run a sweep for hard-coded pixel sizes.

review.reason: Native menu and preferences captures show large labels with small accelerators/checkboxes. Phrase 'only fonts' is too broad: custom icons also scale, but FlatLaf metrics are not coordinated.

findings.title: Parts picker tiles are fixed 68x62 px: captions clipped at 1.25/1.6, gone at 2.0/2.5, ambiguous at 1.0

originalClaim.surface: Library side panel (component palette)
originalClaim.observed:
At 1.6 every caption is cut horizontally through the middle ('NOT', 'Buffer', 'AND' show only their top half).

The caption uses UiFonts.small() (scaled) and is drawn at PREVIEW_HEIGHT+Spacing.sm()+ascent (~lines 180-186), below the component's bottom edge. findings.title: Side panel, inspector and bottom panel widths are raw device pixels, so panels shrink relative to content at high scales

findings.title: First launch runs the legacy layout 'migration', so the side panel is permanently 25% of a half-screen window (170 px on 1366x768: one-column palette)

It then multiplies the default WINDOW_MAIN_SPLIT fraction by the default window width (screen width/2, AppPreferences.java:1312-1319) and persists the result.

findings.title: Changing the scale ('Zoom factor') applies half-live: mixed-size UI, misleading restart text, no value shown, no restart action

originalClaim.title: Changing the scale ('Zoom factor') applies half-live: mixed-size UI, misleading restart text, no value shown, no restart action
originalClaim.surface: Preferences > Window > Zoom factor slider and 'Set zoom factor to Logisim's default'
originalClaim.observed:
Dragging the slider from 1.6 to 1.0 immediately shrinks toolbar icons, activity-bar icons and palette captions. The menu bar, panel headers, search fields, tabs, welcome text, zoom pill, status bar and the Preferences page stay at 1.6. The Preferences nav list shrinks but its page does not. The 'Set zoom factor to Logisim's default' button produces the same mixed state.

Other problems with the control:
- The static italic warning says 'may have unpredictable results and requires a restart', but offers no restart button.
- The slider shows no current value.
- Range is 1.0x–3.0x only, with a tiny unscaled thumb.
- It is named 'Zoom factor', which collides with canvas zoom (100% pill).
originalClaim.expected: A clearly named 'Interface scale' control (for example a 75–300% dropdown or stepper showing the current value) that either applies fully live or shows a non-blocking 'Restart to apply' banner with a Restart button. Never a mixed state.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/prefs/WindowOptions.java:106-124 builds the JTextArea warning and the ZoomSlider (100..300). stateChanged (:272-284) sets SCALE_FACTOR and only revalidates the frames. Code that reads UiScale at paint time (AppIcons, UiFonts, Spacing) updates; fonts set once by the AWT re-font hack do not. The reset button (:318-323) does the same. Strings: windowToolbarZoomfactor and windowToolbarImportant in gui.properties.
originalClaim.fixIdea: After scaling-01, apply live: update flatlaf.uiScale, then FlatLaf.updateUI(), AppIcons.clearCache() and revalidate all windows. Otherwise persist the value and show an explicit 'Restart now' affordance. Rename the control, show a percentage, allow values below 100%, and drop the scary copy.

review.reason: Live 2.0->1.0 slider/Home change shrinks captions and toolbar glyphs while menu, headers, fields and cached previews retain old sizes. Restart warning exists; no dynamic restart action.

findings.title: Canvas '100%' ignores the interface scale: circuits render at half the UI text size at 1.6 (a third at 2.5), with hairline strokes

originalClaim.title: Canvas '100%' ignores the interface scale: circuits render at half the UI text size at 1.6 (a third at 2.5), with hairline strokes
originalClaim.surface: Circuit canvas at default zoom
originalClaim.observed: At the user's 1.6, component labels ('b in', 'b out', pin values '0') are about 8–9 physical px, while the tab label beside them is about 16 px; wires and outlines are 1–2 px hairlines. At 2.5 the canvas is identical to 1.0 while the UI around it is 2.5x. The circuit sits as a tiny island in the top-left of a huge canvas.
originalClaim.expected: Canvas zoom 100% maps to the UI scale, so a 12 pt canvas label matches 12 pt UI text. Stroke widths scale too.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Frame.java:256 creates BasicZoomModel with zoomFactor 1.0 (gui/generic/BasicZoomModel.java:34). The Canvas transform does not multiply by SCALE_FACTOR, and Java2D's own scale is 1 under Xwayland.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Apply device zoom = userZoom × UiScale.factor() in the canvas transform (and Appearance editor, printing excluded), while the pill keeps showing the user zoom (100%).

review.reason: UI scale and document zoom are intentionally separate. Changing circuit fonts/geometry with theme would violate UiFonts' document-font contract. Evaluate default viewport zoom separately; no blanket canvas-scale bug.

findings.title: Preferences 'Filter settings' only matches page titles: 'scale', 'zoom' and 'theme' find nothing and leave a blank list

The splash progress text 'Initializing interface...' is about 9 px and runs into the edge of the bar. The scrollbar is 12 px and the split dividers are 5 px.
originalClaim.expected: One consistent scale, so that fonts, insets, icons, row heights, arrows, check marks, caption buttons and dividers all grow together.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:1161-1190: an AWT ContainerListener forces the font of every added JLabel, JMenuItem, JButton, JToolTip and so on to AppPreferences.getScaledFont (14 * 1.6). FlatLaf's own UIScale is never set: no 'flatlaf.uiScale' system property or UIScale call anywhere, and Main.java:79-113 only swaps the font family. So everything FlatLaf.properties defines (Tree.rowHeight=24, Table.rowHeight=24, TabbedPane.tabHeight=32, ScrollBar.width=12, SplitPane.dividerSize=5, MenuItem.acceleratorFont, CheckBox/RadioButton icons, TitlePane button size, TitledBorder font) stays at 1x.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Before the look and feel is installed, set System.setProperty("flatlaf.uiScale", scale) (or UIScale.setZoomFactor) and set the default font through UIManager 'defaultFont'. Delete the Startup AWT font listener and AppPreferences.setScaledFonts. Keep UiScale.factor() in step with FlatLaf's scale so the hand-painted components use the same number.

review.title: FlatLaf metrics stay at 1x while fonts are forced to 1.6x: tiny accelerators, arrows, check marks, checkboxes, window buttons; clipped rows
review.reason: Live Edit popup and Save dialog visibly mix large labels with small accelerators/icons; archived drawer also shows small captions. HEAD retains post-construction font scaling. Do not infer that every reported widget was retested, or prescribe a particular FlatLaf API without validating double scaling.

findings.title: None of the three splitters (side panel, inspector, drawer) can be dragged

originalClaim.title: None of the three splitters (side panel, inspector, drawer) can be dragged
originalClaim.surface: Side panel / editor divider, editor / inspector divider, canvas / bottom drawer divider
originalClaim.observed: I dragged each divider from every x (or y) position across its 5 px band, both slowly in steps and quickly. The panel never changed size, either during the drag or after release. The hit target is also only 5 device px (about 3 logical px) wide.
originalClaim.expected: The dividers should resize live with the pointer, show a resize cursor over a hit area of 6-8 logical px, and remember the new size.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/ShellLayout.java:201-216. SizedSplit.doLayout re-applies the stored size on every layout. With continuousLayout=true (line 120), every drag step calls setDividerLocation, then revalidate, then doLayout, which snaps the divider back to the stored size. The mouseReleased hook (172-179) then stores that snapped-back size. DIVIDER_SIZE = 5 at line 31 is unscaled.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Enforce the stored size only until the first real layout, or while the window is resizing, and skip enforcement while the divider is being dragged. Simpler: set the divider location once in addNotify/componentResized and update the stored size in a PropertyChangeListener on DIVIDER_LOCATION_PROPERTY. Scale the divider size.

review.title: None of the three splitters (side panel, inspector, drawer) can be dragged
review.reason: Side and inspector divider drags failed to retain the requested hundreds-of-pixels change; inspector shifted only about five pixels. doLayout reapplies stored size during drag. Drawer was not dragged live; it uses the same SizedSplit path.

corroborations.title: Drawer and panel resizing snaps back; default timing/test-vector content is unusably short
corroborations.verification: Fresh live divider drags and vector run, backed by source.
corroborations.observed: Both tested divider positions remain unchanged after dragging. Timing shows only the ruler; loaded test vectors report 2 passed/2 failed but have no visible result rows at the default drawer height.
reproduction: Open Timing diagram and select clk.
Drag the drawer divider upward and the Circuits divider rightward.
Open inv > Test Vector and load the copied inv_test.txt.
corroborations.rootCause: Continuous split layout reapplies the remembered size before drag release can persist the new size. Drawer migration/minimum is in unscaled pixels, so the existing height is inadequate at 1.6.
corroborations.fix: Apply restored sizes during initialization/explicit relayout only, permit live dragging, and persist the released size. Derive the drawer's initial/minimum useful height from its controls and font metrics; keep body scrolling available.
corroborations.acceptance: At 1.0, 1.6 and 2.0 scales, drag every splitter smoothly, reopen with sizes retained, and inspect a visible waveform plus at least four test rows. A 2-pass/2-fail vector exposes each failed cell and Show/Set actions.
corroborations.reason: Same shared splitter defect as shell-03. Hidden timing/test rows are downstream effects, not two extra bugs.

findings.title: Once closed, the Properties panel can only come back through Preferences > Window > 'Reset window layout to Logisim's defaults'

originalClaim.title: Once closed, the Properties panel can only come back through Preferences > Window > 'Reset window layout to Logisim's defaults'
originalClaim.surface: Properties inspector close x; Window menu; activity bar
originalClaim.observed: Clicking the inspector's x hides it and saves that choice. The Window menu has no Properties item, there is no right-hand activity icon, no shortcut and no status-bar toggle. The only way back is Preferences > Window > Reset window layout, which also resets every other panel size. The STATE section disappears along with it.
originalClaim.expected: The panel should be restorable where the user looks for it: Window > Appearance > Properties (for example Ctrl+Alt+P), a toggle in the toolbar or status bar, or a right-edge activity strip, like VS Code's secondary sidebar or JetBrains tool windows. The same applies to the bottom drawer and the side panel.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Frame.java:372 wires inspector.setOnClose to shell.setInspectorVisible(false). The only caller that turns it back on is ShellLayout.resetLayout, reached through gui/prefs/WindowOptions.java:315. util/WindowMenu.java has only the legacy Toolbar and Navigation Pane toggles.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Add a 'View' or 'Window > Panels' group with checkable Side Panel, Properties and Drawer items plus shortcuts, bound to ShellLayout. Add small toggle buttons at the ends of the status bar (as VS Code does). Offer 'Reset Layout' as a menu command instead of a Preferences button.

review.title: Once closed, the Properties panel can only come back through Preferences > Window > 'Reset window layout to Logisim's defaults'
review.reason: The normal Show Properties path only changes the attribute model; inspector visibility true is restored by reset/initial preference restoration, not that command. No live hide/reset cycle was needed after source tracing. Missing direct restore blocks the normal inspector workflow until layout reset.

findings.title: Panel widths and heights are fixed in unscaled pixels, so every panel is too narrow at 1.6x and truncates its content

originalClaim.title: Panel widths and heights are fixed in unscaled pixels, so every panel is too narrow at 1.6x and truncates its content
originalClaim.surface: Side panel (260 px), inspector (280 px), bottom drawer (200 px)
originalClaim.observed: At 1.6x the side panel is about 160 logical px wide. The Circuits header shows 'CI…'; the library search placeholder is 'Search compone…'; the parts grid fits only 3 columns. The inspector truncates every property name: 'FPGA supp…', 'Number Of…', 'Negate 1 (…', 'Negate 2 (…', and two different rows both read 'Shared Lab…'. 'Output Value0/1' runs label into value, and 'Label Font SansSerif B…' is cut. The drawer shows one row of its content: the Timing 'Options' page is cut off below 'Add or Remove' and 'Capture fine-grained details'. In a 1706 px window the drawer's button renders as 'd or Remo'.
originalClaim.expected: Default and minimum panel sizes in logical units scaled by the UI factor (for example side 280, inspector 300, drawer 240 logical). Headers and values should get tooltips when truncated, and inspector rows should wrap or ellipsize from the middle.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/LayoutPrefs.java:26-43 (MIN_PANEL=160, MAX_PANEL=720, DEFAULT_SIDE_WIDTH=260, DEFAULT_INSPECTOR_WIDTH=280, DEFAULT_BOTTOM_HEIGHT=200) are device pixels and are never scaled. ShellLayout.java:87-89 uses them as minimum sizes. The palette tile size is the same class of bug.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Store and restore these values in logical px and multiply by UiScale when applying (divide when saving). Enforce a minimum inspector name column, add a resizable column split, and set a tooltip on any truncated cell or header.

review.title: Panel widths and heights are fixed in unscaled pixels, so every panel is too narrow at 1.6x and truncates its content
review.reason: Live inspector truncates names and font values at 1.6 scale; LayoutPrefs retains device-pixel defaults. Fresh Circuits width was wider and its heading readable, so not every panel is always truncated. Separate this sizing defect from the divider interaction defect.

findings.title: Properties inspector table is a raw legacy JTable: neon-green 'Supported' cell, no padding, a blank box when empty, raw coordinates in the header

originalClaim.title: Properties inspector table is a raw legacy JTable: neon-green 'Supported' cell, no padding, a blank box when empty, raw coordinates in the header
originalClaim.surface: Properties inspector (empty, with a component selected, with circuit attributes)
originalClaim.observed: The first row of every component is 'FPGA supp…', with a pure #00FF00 cell and black 'Supported' text. Labels start flush against the box border with no left padding, and rows have no separators. Values don't look editable: no combo arrows or text-field affordance. The header is 'NAND GATE (160,140)', raw grid coordinates in caps. With nothing selected on a new or empty circuit, the panel is an empty bordered grey box with no message. After a click on a circuit in the list, the same state shows 'CIRCUIT: CPU' attributes, which is inconsistent. The inset box border doesn't line up with the header text. The close x has no hover state.
originalClaim.expected: A property grid like JetBrains or Figma: grouped sections, 8-12 px padding, a muted label column and editable-looking value controls. FPGA support should be a small status pill in theme colours (or live in an 'HDL' section). Empty state: 'Select a component to edit its properties' plus the circuit's properties. The header should show the component name, with the location in muted text.
originalClaim.rootCause: fpga/gui/HdlColorRenderer.java:103-106 (Color.RED / Color.GREEN). gui/generic/AttrTable.java:100-106 puts the table in a default bordered JScrollPane with no cell insets. gui/shell/Inspector.java:52-58 has a close button with contentAreaFilled=false and no hover. Frame.inspectorTitle (Frame.java:820-825) shows the title from the model, which includes the location.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Restyle AttrTable: remove the scroll border, add cell padding, use Tokens for the FPGA badge (subtle success or error pill), make value editors look editable, add an empty-state label, and default to circuit attributes when nothing is selected.

review.title: Properties inspector table is a raw legacy JTable: neon-green 'Supported' cell, no padding, a blank box when empty, raw coordinates in the header
review.reason: Compound inspector styling claim: FPGA fill overlaps inspector-03; padding overlaps inspector-13 and empty state inspector-10. No separate shell defect.

findings.title: Editor tab overflow hides the active tab, with no scroll arrows or overflow list

originalClaim.title: Editor tab overflow hides the active tab, with no scroll arrows or overflow list
originalClaim.surface: Editor tab strip
originalClaim.observed: With 14 circuits open, the strip shows 'main' through 'Merger16' in one row, clipped at the inspector. The active tab (ALU) is not visible anywhere. Only a sliver of its blue underline peeks out at the far right. There are no scroll buttons and no chevron list.
originalClaim.expected: Scroll layout that keeps the selected tab visible, plus an overflow (chevron) menu listing every open tab, as in VS Code and JetBrains.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/EditorTabs.java:53-62. The tab layout policy is never set to JTabbedPane.SCROLL_TAB_LAYOUT; the FlatLaf scroll-button and tabsPopup properties (EditorTabs:57-58, FlatLaf.properties:33-34) only apply in scroll layout. With WRAP layout, getComponentAt returning null (210-215) and the strip in EditorArea NORTH, the wrapped rows are clipped. rebuild() does removeAll/addTab on every change, which also resets scrolling.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Call setTabLayoutPolicy(SCROLL_TAB_LAYOUT) and set TABBED_PANE_TABS_POPUP_POLICY to asNeeded. Update tabs incrementally instead of rebuilding, and call ensure-visible on the selected tab.

review.title: Editor tab overflow hides the active tab, with no scroll arrows or overflow list
review.reason: Reviewed the original overflow strip: clipped tabs without usable overflow controls. HEAD sets scroll-button policy but not SCROLL_TAB_LAYOUT. Original active-ALU context is inherited from the report; no new 14-tab live reproduction.

findings.title: Closing the last tab leaves the circuit on screen with no tab; the circuit list selection goes stale

originalClaim.title: Closing the last tab leaves the circuit on screen with no tab; the circuit list selection goes stale
originalClaim.surface: Editor tabs and Circuits list
originalClaim.observed: I right-clicked COR and chose Close Others, which left the COR tab, while the Circuits list still highlighted ALU. Clicking the tab's x closed it: the tab strip disappeared and the canvas jumped up, but COR stayed displayed and editable, the title still read 'COR of PC', and the list still highlighted ALU.
originalClaim.expected: With no tabs open, show an empty-editor state (for example 'Open a circuit from the Circuits panel', with shortcuts). The list selection must always match the active tab.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/shell/EditorTabs.java:184 only hides the strip (setVisible(getTabCount() > 0)), and the Frame keeps project.getCurrentCircuit(). CircuitListView does not follow EditorTabModel selection changes made by Close Others. Exact listener not traced.
originalClaim.fixIdea: When the model has zero tabs, switch mainPanel to an empty-editor card. Make CircuitListView observe EditorTabModel (or project circuit changes) and select the matching row.

review.title: Closing the last tab leaves the circuit on screen with no tab; the circuit list selection goes stale
review.reason: Closing the sole tab live removed its strip while leaving the gate editable and project title intact. Circuit-list staleness after Close Others was not independently reproduced.

findings.title: The welcome screen covers a project that is already open; 'New project' opens a second window; the project's own circuit can't be reached

originalClaim.title: The welcome screen covers a project that is already open; 'New project' opens a second window; the project's own circuit can't be reached
originalClaim.surface: Welcome screen on startup without a file
originalClaim.observed: At launch the title reads 'main of Untitled'. The Circuits panel lists 'main (main)', the Simulate view lists 'main' as an active simulation, the status bar says 'main  100%', every drawing tool is enabled, and Edit offers 'Undo Load Library'. The editor area, though, shows the welcome page. Clicking or double-clicking 'main' in the Circuits list does not dismiss the welcome. 'New project' creates a SECOND window ('main of Untitled_2') and leaves the original window, still on the welcome page, behind it. Recent-file clicks replace the blank project instead, so the two buttons behave differently. The welcome links have no hover state.
originalClaim.expected: Either no project exists while the welcome shows (tools, circuit list and simulation are empty or disabled), or the welcome is a start tab. 'New project' should reuse the blank window, and choosing the project's circuit should open it. Link rows should highlight on hover and keyboard focus.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/main/Frame.java:299-302: the welcome callbacks use ProjectActions.doNew(project), which always creates a new frame (proj/ProjectActions.java:193-201), while recent files use doOpenReplacingBlank. dismissWelcome (Frame.java:792-799) is reached only through startupScreenChanged(false) (Frame.java:769-775), not by selecting a circuit. The welcome is shown by gui/start/Startup.java:1129-1135 on top of the already-created project.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Make 'New project' dismiss the welcome and reuse the startup blank project, or replace it the way doOpenReplacingBlank does. Dismiss the welcome whenever a circuit is chosen in the list or tabs. Disable project-dependent chrome (tools, simulate view, status) while the welcome shows. Add hover and focus states to WelcomePanel links.

review.title: The welcome screen covers a project that is already open; 'New project' opens a second window; the project's own circuit can't be reached
review.reason: Fresh startup visibly overlays an existing Untitled circuit with Welcome. New callback calls doNew while recent-file callback uses doOpenReplacingBlank. Second-window and circuit-click recovery details are source/reported evidence, not a clean independent live comparison.

findings.title: A new project starts with an invisible 'Load Library' undo step

originalClaim.title: A new project starts with an invisible 'Load Library' undo step
originalClaim.surface: Edit menu on a new or startup project
originalClaim.observed: On a pristine Untitled project, Edit shows 'Undo Load Library' and Undo History lists 'Load Library'. Ctrl+Z seems to do nothing, then Edit reads 'Nothing to Undo / Redo Load Library'. This wastes the user's first undo and exposes internals.
originalClaim.expected: Libraries loaded at startup should not be undoable actions. A new project should open with an empty undo stack.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/start/Startup.java:1125-1126 wraps loading the default libraries in proj.doAction(LogisimFileActions.loadLibraries(...)), so it lands on the undo stack. The comment at 1128 confirms it counts as an action.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Add the libraries directly to the LogisimFile (or discard the undo history and mark the file clean) instead of calling proj.doAction.

review.title: A new project starts with an invisible 'Load Library' undo step
review.reason: Startup loads default libraries through proj.doAction, explaining a startup undo entry. No separate pristine Undo-history screenshot captured.

findings.title: Simulation controls float in the middle of the toolbar and jump when tools change or the toolbar is hidden

originalClaim.title: Simulation controls float in the middle of the toolbar and jump when tools change or the toolbar is hidden
originalClaim.surface: Main toolbar
originalClaim.observed: The design says the simulation controls are 'pushed to the far side'. In fact they sit at x≈1490 of 2560 in the default project, x≈1450 in PC.circ (fewer tool buttons), and at the far left after Window > Show Toolbar is unchecked. 'Show Toolbar' hides only the drawing tools and leaves the simulation strip in a different place.
originalClaim.expected: Simulation controls anchored at a fixed spot (the right edge, or centred as a run bar in JetBrains style) that never moves. 'Show Toolbar' should hide the whole row or be removed.
originalClaim.rootCause: draw/toolbar/Toolbar.java:29-36 makes each Toolbar a BorderLayout with an empty JPanel in CENTER, so its maximum width is unbounded. In MainToolbar's X_AXIS BoxLayout (gui/shell/MainToolbar.java:45-51), the extra width is shared between the glue, 'tools' and 'simulation', and the simulation buttons are left-aligned inside their stretched panel.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Give Toolbar getMaximumSize() = getPreferredSize() (or drop the CENTER filler), or lay out MainToolbar with BorderLayout (tools WEST, simulation EAST). Make 'Show Toolbar' hide the whole MainToolbar.

review.title: Simulation controls float in the middle of the toolbar and jump when tools change or the toolbar is hidden
review.reason: Live full-window screenshots show simulation controls starting well before the right edge with large unused toolbar space. Hide-toolbar jump not retested; alignment is usability polish.

findings.title: Toolbar mixes 2005 pixel-art tool icons with thin line icons; simulation buttons have no hover and aren't focusable

originalClaim.title: Toolbar mixes 2005 pixel-art tool icons with thin line icons; simulation buttons have no hover and aren't focusable
originalClaim.surface: Main toolbar and Simulate side-view strip
originalClaim.observed: The drawing tools are the classic Logisim bitmaps: skin-tone pointing hand, bold serif 'A', a landscape 'image' icon, filled black/white flip-flop and register glyphs, pin arrows with green dashes. The simulation buttons use thin Lucide-style outlines. Tool buttons show a rounded hover background; the simulation buttons show none. The separators are tiny grey 3 px squares. The 'Stop simulator' button is a yellow pause icon that reads as a warning state.
originalClaim.expected: One icon family (the line icons already in AppIcons) at one stroke weight, drawn by theme tokens. The same hover, pressed and focus states on every toolbar button. Clear run/pause state (for example a green play or red stop).
originalClaim.rootCause: draw/toolbar/ToolbarButton.java:62-63 computes 'interactive' once at construction from item.isSelectable(). LogisimToolbarItem.isSelectable (gui/main/LogisimToolbarItem.java:81-83) is false while the menu action is disabled at build time, so the simulation buttons never get rollover or focus. The tool icons come from each tool's legacy getIcon/paintIcon (gui/icons/*, std/*).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Compute rollover and focusability dynamically (or always true for clickable items). Replace the tool icons with SVGs from AppIcons, and replace the separator item with a 1 px vertical divider.

review.title: Toolbar mixes 2005 pixel-art tool icons with thin line icons; simulation buttons have no hover and aren't focusable
review.reason: Mixed legacy and line icon styles are visible. Replacement is a design decision; missing hover/focus behavior was not independently tested.

findings.title: Tooltip and terminology inconsistencies between the toolbar, the menus and the tooltips themselves

originalClaim.title: Tooltip and terminology inconsistencies between the toolbar, the menus and the tooltips themselves
originalClaim.surface: Toolbar tooltips, Simulate menu, side-panel header tooltips, zoom pill
originalClaim.observed: Both pin tools say 'Add Pin' ('Add Pin (Ctrl+6)' and 'Add Pin (Ctrl+7)'), so input and output can't be told apart. Capitalisation is mixed: 'Add Image', 'Add NOT Gate' vs 'Add and edit labels', 'Draw wires between components'. Simulation tooltips drop their shortcuts and use different names from the menu: 'Stop simulator' vs 'Auto-Propagate', 'Step simulator once' vs 'Single-Step Propagation', 'Enable clock ticks' vs 'Auto-Tick Enabled', 'Tick clock one half cycle' vs 'Manual Tick Half Cycle'. Circuits header tooltips mix 'New circuit' and 'New VHDL Entity…'. The zoom-pill fit button says 'Auto', and 'Show grid' doesn't change when the grid is on.
originalClaim.expected: One glossary (for example Run / Pause simulation, Step, Clock: Start / Stop, Tick ½ / Tick 1). Sentence-case tooltips, each with its shortcut. 'Input pin' / 'Output pin'. 'Zoom to fit'. A toggle label that reflects the grid state.
originalClaim.rootCause: Strings in resources/logisim/strings/gui/gui.properties and std bundles (the tool 'Add %s' tooltips come from factory display names, and both pins share the name 'Pin'). gui/main/SimulationToolbarModel.java tooltips. gui/shell/ZoomPill.java.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Write a terminology table and apply it to menus, tooltips and Find Action. Append KeyStroke text to every tooltip automatically from the bound menu accelerator.

review.title: Tooltip and terminology inconsistencies between the toolbar, the menus and the tooltips themselves
review.reason: Unify command names, distinguish pin presets, and rename Auto to Fit to contents. Other tooltip/shortcut claims remain reported rather than independently inspected.

findings.title: Menus keep 2005-era wording, duplicates and inconsistent capitalisation

originalClaim.title: Menus keep 2005-era wording, duplicates and inconsistent capitalisation
originalClaim.surface: File, Edit, Project, Simulate and Window menus, and Open Recent
originalClaim.observed:
- **Old wording:** 'Nothing to Redo' / 'Nothing to Undo' instead of disabled Undo/Redo; 'Ctrl+Comma' instead of 'Ctrl+,'; 'Merge…'; 'Go Out To State' / 'Go In To State'; 'Show Navigation Pane'; 'Test Vector…'.
- **Mixed case:** 'Restart VHDL simulator', 'Timing diagram', 'Assembly viewer' (sentence case) next to 'Revert To Default Appearance', 'Set As Main Circuit' (title case).
- **Ellipsis plus submenu:** 'Built-in Library…' has both an ellipsis and a submenu arrow, and its submenu holds only 'HDL-IP'.
- **Duplicates:** Window > Close duplicates File > Close with the same Ctrl+Shift+W. Window > Preferences (no ellipsis) duplicates File > Preferences…. Window > Circuit Analysis duplicates Project > Analyze Circuit.
- **Menu contents:** Appearance-editor-only items (Bring Forward/Backward, Add/Remove Vertex) are always in Edit, disabled. 'Clear Undo/Redo History' is a top-level Edit item.
- **Frequencies:** listed as '2048.0 kHz', '1.0 Hz' instead of '2.048 MHz', '1 Hz'.
- **Open Recent:** paths are truncated inconsistently ('…/scratchpad/sample.circ', '…/assignement_2.circ', '/home/nilsb/Downloads/PC.circ'), unlike the welcome list, and there is no 'Clear Recent'.
originalClaim.expected: Modern menu copy: Undo/Redo with the action name when available, 'Ctrl+,', sentence or title case applied consistently, no duplicate commands, context-specific items only where they apply, humanised frequencies, and recent items as 'name — ~/dir' plus 'Clear Recently Opened'.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/menu/MenuEdit.java, MenuFile.java:104-105 (shares HOTKEY_WINDOW_CLOSE), util/WindowMenu.java:117-122, gui/menu/OpenRecent.java (shortest-unique-suffix labels), gui/menu/MenuSimulate.java TickFrequencyChoice, and gui.properties strings (for example 'Nothing to Redo'). The KeyStroke display 'Ctrl+Comma' comes from AWT KeyEvent text.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Audit the menu strings in gui.properties. Remove the Window > Close / Preferences / Circuit Analysis duplicates, and show appearance items only in the appearance editor. Format frequencies with SI prefixes. Show recent items as 'name — ~/path', and add a Clear item.

review.title: Menus keep 2005-era wording, duplicates and inconsistent capitalisation
review.reason: Live Edit popup confirms disabled appearance commands and verbose Undo wording. These are discoverability/copy choices, not blocked workflows. Other menu subclaims were not retoured.

findings.title: Window > 'Show Navigation Pane' is out of sync with the activity bar; there are no toggles for the inspector, drawer or status bar

originalClaim.title: Window > 'Show Navigation Pane' is out of sync with the activity bar; there are no toggles for the inspector, drawer or status bar
originalClaim.surface: Window menu vs activity bar
originalClaim.observed: I collapsed the side panel by clicking the active activity icon, but Window > Show Navigation Pane stayed checked. The first click on it unchecks it and changes nothing. A second click finally shows the panel.
originalClaim.expected: The menu check state bound to the actual side-panel visibility, under the same name as the rest of the UI ('Side Panel' / 'Primary Side Bar').

review.title: Window > 'Show Navigation Pane' is out of sync with the activity bar; there are no toggles for the inspector, drawer or status bar
review.reason: Not independently reproduced, visually inspected, or source-traced in this bounded review. Retained as a candidate, not counted as a verified defect.

findings.title: Bottom drawer: each tab's x hides the whole drawer, there is no drawer toggle, and the content is legacy (tabs inside tabs, titled borders)

originalClaim.title: Bottom drawer: each tab's x hides the whole drawer, there is no drawer toggle, and the content is legacy (tabs inside tabs, titled borders)
originalClaim.surface: Bottom drawer (VHDL Console, Timing diagram)
originalClaim.observed: Simulate > Timing diagram opens the drawer with the tabs 'VHDL Console ×' and 'Timing diagram ×'. The VHDL Console tab is always there, even when no VHDL is used. Clicking × on Timing diagram hides the entire drawer instead of closing that tab. There is no header, collapse or maximise control, no menu item and no shortcut to reopen it. Inside is a second tab row ('Options | Timing diagram') and etched TitledBorder boxes with tiny captions. At 200 px unscaled height only one row of controls is visible, with no scrollbar reachable.

review.title: Bottom drawer: each tab's x hides the whole drawer, there is no drawer toggle, and the content is legacy (tabs inside tabs, titled borders)
review.reason: BottomPanel close callback hides the entire drawer rather than removing its tab; archived nested controls are visible. The absolute claim that timing cannot reopen is too strong: the same Simulate command is an existing entry point.

findings.title: STATE section expands to nothing (or a bare 'Name | Value' JTable header) with no empty state

originalClaim.title: STATE section expands to nothing (or a bare 'Name | Value' JTable header) with no empty state
originalClaim.surface: Inspector > STATE

findings.title: ConcurrentModificationException in hotkeySync on the preferences thread

originalClaim.title: ConcurrentModificationException in hotkeySync on the preferences thread
originalClaim.surface: App log after opening Preferences and creating or closing project windows
originalClaim.observed: 'Exception in thread "Event Dispatch Thread" java.util.ConcurrentModificationException at AppPreferences.hotkeySync(AppPreferences.java:1712) at HotkeyOptions.lambda$new$1(HotkeyOptions.java:195) at java.util.prefs.AbstractPreferences$EventDispatchThread.run'. Every preference change (window size, layout, theme) triggers a full hotkey re-sync of every menu, off the Swing thread.
originalClaim.expected: No exceptions. Menu accelerators should update on the EDT, and only when a hotkey preference changes.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/prefs/HotkeyOptions.java:195 adds a PreferenceChangeListener, per HotkeyOptions instance and never removed, that calls AppPreferences.hotkeySync(). That method iterates the plain ArrayList gui_sync_objects (AppPreferences.java:1704-1712) on java.util.prefs' dispatcher thread while the EDT adds menus to it (util/WindowMenu.java:124, LogisimMenuBar) as windows open and close.
originalClaim.fixIdea: Filter to hotkey keys only, marshal to the EDT with SwingUtilities.invokeLater, use a CopyOnWriteArrayList (or weak set) for gui_sync_objects, and remove the listener when the Preferences window closes.

review.title: ConcurrentModificationException in hotkeySync on the preferences thread

corroborations.title: Hotkey synchronization races the preferences dispatcher
corroborations.verification: Recovered HDL log inspected; not triggered in the current fresh session.

findings.title: 'Follow system' theme polls the desktop every 20 s by starting two gsettings processes on the event thread

originalClaim.title: 'Follow system' theme polls the desktop every 20 s by starting two gsettings processes on the event thread
originalClaim.surface: Whole UI when Theme = System
originalClaim.observed: Theme.updateSystemPoll starts a javax.swing.Timer, so it fires on the EDT, and the timer calls apply(Mode.SYSTEM) every 20 s. That calls SystemTheme.isSystemDark(), which on Linux runs `gsettings get ... color-scheme` and `gsettings get ... gtk-theme` synchronously before reading kdeglobals. On KDE both gsettings calls return nothing useful, so both processes are paid for on every tick. SystemTheme.run() reads stdout to EOF before its 2 s waitFor timeout, so a hung gsettings/dconf freezes the whole UI with no upper bound. Not visually verified.
originalClaim.expected: Probe off the EDT (SwingWorker or executor) and apply the result on the EDT only when it changed. Prefer an event source (XSETTINGS / portal color-scheme) over polling.
originalClaim.rootCause: gui/theme/Theme.java:61 (SYSTEM_POLL_MS 20000), :176-192 (Swing Timer calling apply). gui/theme/SystemTheme.java:58-70 (two gsettings probes before kdeglobals), :162-181 (blocking readLine before waitFor).
originalClaim.fixIdea: Run SystemTheme.isSystemDark() on a background executor, compare it with the cached value, and invokeLater apply() only when it differs. On KDE, check kdeglobals first.

review.reason: Swing Timer invokes theme detection on EDT; SystemTheme.run reads to EOF before its timeout. UI freeze risk under a hung probe is credible but was not induced.

originalClaim.observed: With main and inv open, canvas focus followed by Ctrl+Tab left main selected. With three tabs open, Ctrl+Shift+Tab from inv left inv selected. Ctrl+W from the same canvas successfully closed inv.
reproduction: Open at least two circuits from the Circuits list.
Click empty canvas to give it focus.
Press Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab; compare active editor tabs.

originalClaim.rootCause: The shortcuts are installed in the tab strip's WHEN_IN_FOCUSED_WINDOW map. No corresponding focus-traversal override was found on Canvas/EditorTabs. Traversal interception is the likely cause, not yet instrumented; live failure is established.
originalClaim.fix: Trace the focus manager's consumed key events and route next/previous-editor actions at the owning root pane/focus boundary, excluding those chords from traversal where necessary. Keep ordinary Tab and text-editor behavior intact.
originalClaim.acceptance: At least three circuit/HDL tabs wrap forward and backward from canvas, circuit list, filter, and code editor focus. Ctrl+W still closes one tab; normal Tab traverses controls with visible focus.
originalClaim.limits: Window-manager and platform portability beyond the private Linux KWin/Xwayland session is untested.

findings.title: SoC transaction dialog identifies the target bus as null

originalClaim.title: SoC transaction dialog identifies the target bus as null

originalClaim.observed: The dialog title reads Insert a transaction to bus: null, although the memory-map window can identify the bus.

originalClaim.rootCause: actionPerformed passes info.getName(), the inherited JMenuItem component name. The constructors call super(label) but never set that name. The resulting null is concatenated into the window title.

findings.title: System-theme timeout does not bound subprocess output reads

originalClaim.title: System-theme timeout does not bound subprocess output reads
originalClaim.observed: SystemTheme.run waits for readLine EOF before the timed waitFor. A silent three-second process completes successfully after 3004ms despite a two-second timeout. Theme's Swing Timer invokes this path on the EDT; an unresponsive desktop command can freeze the UI.
originalClaim.fix: Move desktop discovery off EDT, bound the whole subprocess lifetime including output collection, cap output and cancel/kill timed-out children. Apply only the latest result on EDT.
originalClaim.acceptance: A silent or never-ending test process respects the deadline; typing and repainting remain responsive during the probe. No physical OS-theme hang was reproduced in this audit.

findings.title: Palette rebuilds retain discarded tiles through strong theme listeners

originalClaim.title: Palette rebuilds retain discarded tiles through strong theme listeners
originalClaim.observed: Each ComponentTile registers this::repaint in Theme's static strong listener list. findings.title: Automatic OS-theme changes bypass the canvas palette refresh path

originalClaim.title: Automatic OS-theme changes bypass the canvas palette refresh path
originalClaim.observed: The System Theme timer calls Theme.apply, which changes LaF and fires listeners. AppPreferences.applyThemeColors and refreshProjectsForTheme are only called separately by the preference combo and startup; the automatic path has no equivalent palette update.
originalClaim.fix: Use one ordered theme transaction for startup, preference changes and OS notifications: resolve mode, load theme-specific palette, update UI and editors, repaint all document views, notify listeners on EDT.
originalClaim.acceptance: A simulated OS-theme change updates chrome, canvas, values, diagram, editor and cached previews together; explicit user colours remain preserved. Physical OS-switch path remains to be tested.

findings.title: Recovered QA harness does not fully isolate home or faithfully capture all window sizes

originalClaim.title: Recovered QA harness does not fully isolate home or faithfully capture all window sizes
originalClaim.observed: Original qa.sh isolates preferences but not user.home, while unnamed autosaves use user.home. originalClaim.fix: Isolate home, prefs, documents and autosaves; validate session IDs/PIDs; never recursively reset a broad/unvalidated path; capture actual window geometry and stacking or native compositor output. Archive metadata and unscaled crops. Preserve existing user recents/autosaves.
originalClaim.acceptance: QA leaves user preference and autosave checksums unchanged, refuses unsafe session IDs and stale PIDs, and captures 1280x800 and 2560x1600 without artificial clipping.
